definition_zh: 抢劫；盗取；剥夺
definition_en: to steal from a person or place, or to take something away unfairly
core_image: 深夜被撬开的后门
scene: 深夜，两名男子撬开商店后门行窃。 Two men broke in through the back door and robbed the shop.

senses.title: Stealing by force
senses.definition: to take money or property from a person or place

senses.example: They robbed the shop at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们半夜抢劫了这家店。

senses.why: Loss can feel like a theft by life itself.
senses.whyCN: 失去感觉就像被生活本身偷走。

intro.cn: rob 源自古法语 rober，意为掠夺。

items.en: Rober means to plunder.
items.cn: rober 意为掠夺。

items.en: Rob enters English as a verb of theft.
items.cn: rob 以盗窃动词进入英语。

items.en: Robber and robbery grow beside it.

items.cn: rob someone of something 意为剥夺。

normal.en: Rob a bank means take its money.
normal.cn: rob a bank 意为抢走银行的钱。

normal.en: Rob someone of sleep means keep them awake.

normal.en: A robber is the person who robs.

normal.en: Remember: rob a place, steal a thing.

abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中后门被推开。

examples.cn: 有人在公交车上抢了这位老人的东西。

examples.en: The war robbed the town of its young people.

branches.cn: 疾病也能在没有窃贼的情况下夺走东西。

definition_zh: 一英镑（英国俚语）；一剂咀嚼的烟草；一句话（短语 quid pro quo）
definition_en: one pound sterling in British slang; a wad of chewing tobacco; a word used in the phrase quid pro quo
core_image: 伦敦小店里一枚硬币被推过柜台，换来一份日报
scene: 伦敦的一家小报摊上，顾客掏出一枚硬币放在柜台上，摊主把卷好的报纸递了过去。 He asked the vendor for a paper and handed over a single quid.
sceneCN: 这里 quid 是「一英镑」（第 1 个义项：英国俚语中的英镑单位）；句意为向摊主要一份报纸并递上一英镑。画面里可留意：报纸摊、柜台上的一枚硬币、一次简单的交易。

pos.zh: 一英镑（英国俚语）；一剂咀嚼的烟草

derivatives.zh: 拉丁短语借词，指「以一物换一物」的交换条件
拉丁语 quid 加 nunc（如今）构成，指爱打听、搬弄是非的人
quid 作动词加 -ing，指咀嚼烟草的旧用法

senses.title: One pound sterling
senses.definition: one pound of British money, in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 一英镑，属英国口语俚语说法
senses.example: The book cost me five quid.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书花了我五英镑。
senses.why: Britons took a neutral Latin word for something or a piece of something and gave it the friendly slang value of the everyday coin they trade with.
senses.whyCN: 英国人借来一个中性的拉丁词（原意为「某物；一份」），把日常使用的硬币赋予了亲切的俚语价值。

senses.title: A wad of chewing tobacco
senses.definition: a small piece of tobacco kept in the mouth for chewing, in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 含在口中咀嚼的一小块烟草，属非正式用法
senses.example: He kept a quid of tobacco in his cheek.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一块烟草含在腮帮里。
senses.why: The same Latin idea of a single piece or portion was applied to the lump of tobacco held in the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「一份、一块」的拉丁概念，被用来指含在嘴里的那一团烟草。

senses.title: A thing given in exchange
senses.titleCN: 交换之物（拉丁短语成分）
senses.definition: a thing or something, in the borrowed Latin phrase quid pro quo, meaning an exchange of one thing for another
senses.definitionCN: 在拉丁借语 quid pro quo 中指「某物」，整个短语意为以一物换另一物
senses.example: They offered a contract with a clear quid pro quo.
senses.exampleCN: 他们提出一份有明确交换条件的合同。
senses.why: In Latin quid was the neuter pronoun meaning what or something, so quid pro quo literally says something for something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语里 quid 是中时代词，意为「什么、某物」，quid pro quo 字面即「以物换物」。

intro.en: Quid is a Latin word meaning something or a piece of something; English borrowed it twice, once as slang for a pound coin and once inside a legal Latin phrase.
intro.cn: quid 是拉丁语中意为「某物；一份」的词；英语两次借入它，一次作为英镑的俚语，一次出现在拉丁法律短语中。

items.en: Quid was the neuter form of the pronoun quis, meaning what or something; it also served as a noun for a piece or portion.
items.cn: quid 是代词 quis 的中性形式，意为「什么、某物」；也用作名词，指一份、一块。

items.en: In pharmacy and law, quid pro quo meant one medicine or thing substituted for another.
items.cn: 在药学与法律语境中，quid pro quo 意为以一种药或一物替代另一物。

items.en: The phrase quid pro quo entered English in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries as a legal term for an exchange.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪，quid pro quo 作为法律术语进入英语，指交换条件。

items.en: By the late seventeenth century quid was street slang for a guinea, and after decimal talk it settled on the pound; the exact reason for the coin link is uncertain.
items.cn: 至十七世纪晚期，quid 已是基尼币的街头俚语，后来落到英镑上；其与货币挂钩的确切缘由不确定。

items.en: In American English the noun quid also meant a wad of chewing tobacco, from the sense of a single piece.
items.cn: 在美国英语中，quid 也指一剂咀嚼烟草，取「一块」之义。

items.en: Today quid means a pound in British speech, a wad of tobacco in older American use, and keeps its place inside quid pro quo.
items.cn: 如今 quid 在英国口语指一英镑，在旧美国用法指一剂烟草，并继续活在 quid pro quo 这个短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers money words that sound close to quid; the near-meaning group gathers currency terms and exchange words.
note.cn: 形近组收与 quid 发音相近的钱币词；近义组收货币单位与交换相关词语。

entries.definition: To stop doing something or to leave a job.
entries.definitionCN: 停止做某事或辞职，与 quid 拼写发音相近但词义无关。

entries.definition: Making little noise and staying calm.
entries.definitionCN: 安静的，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A large feather used as a pen, or a porcupine spine.
entries.definitionCN: 羽毛笔或豪猪刺，与 quid 发音相近但来源不同。

entries.definition: The standard unit of British money.
entries.definitionCN: 英镑，quid 的正式说法。

entries.definition: One dollar in American slang.
entries.definitionCN: 一美元的美国俚语，与 quid 同为口语货币单位。

entries.definition: An old British coin worth twenty-one shillings.
entries.definitionCN: 旧英国金币基尼，quid 俚语义的早期所指。

entries.definition: A balance reached by giving up one thing for another.
entries.definitionCN: 权衡取舍，与 quid pro quo 的交换义相关。

normalIntro.en: A Latin word for something became the British way to say a pound, and a piece of tobacco, and half of a famous phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 一个意为「某物」的拉丁词，成了英国人说英镑的俚语，成了说烟草的一块，也成了著名短语的一半。

normal.en: Five quid means five pounds: the plural stays quid in money talk.
normal.cn: five quid 即五英镑：谈钱时复数仍写作 quid。

normal.en: Quid pro quo literally means something for something.
normal.cn: quid pro quo 字面意思是「以物换物」。

normal.en: Buck is to dollar as quid is to pound: both are slang coin units.
normal.cn: buck 之于美元，正如 quid 之于英镑：都是硬币的俚语单位。

normal.en: A quid of tobacco is one piece kept in the mouth to chew.
normal.cn: a quid of tobacco 指含在口中咀嚼的一块烟草。

normal.en: The coin slang is informal: write pounds in formal documents.
normal.cn: 硬币俚语属于非正式用语：正式文件应写 pounds。

abstract.en: Every price is a quid pro quo: you give something, you receive something.
abstract.cn: 每一笔价格都是一场以物换物：你给出某物，也得到某物。

abstract.en: A single coin on a counter carries a whole history of borrowed words.
abstract.cn: 柜台上的一枚硬币，承载着一段借词的完整历史。

abstract.en: Slang makes money familiar, and a familiar word makes spending easier.
abstract.cn: 俚语让钱变得亲切，而亲切的词让花钱变得轻快。

examples.en: It only cost a few quid at the market.
examples.cn: 这东西在市场上只花了几个英镑。

examples.en: The deal was a simple quid pro quo between the two companies.
examples.cn: 这笔交易是两家公司之间简单的交换条件。

examples.en: In old novels, the sailor kept a quid of tobacco behind his lip.
examples.cn: 在旧小说里，水手常把一剂烟草含在唇后。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快得」——花钱快得很，一 quid 就是一英镑，记住这个英国俚语。

root: 拉丁语 quid（ quis 的中性形式，意为「什么、某物」；亦作名词指一份、一块）→ 拉丁短语 quid pro quo（以物换物）进入英语法律用语 → 十七世纪起 quid 成为英国货币俚语；货币义的来历一般认为源于拉丁「一份」之义，存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a single piece of something; the senses divide into a pound coin in slang, a wad of chewing tobacco, and the something inside quid pro quo.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「某物的一份」；义项分为俚语中的一英镑、一剂咀嚼烟草，以及 quid pro quo 中的「某物」。

senses.whyCN: 拖延的危险，会变成无法挽回的损失。

senses.title: The turning point
senses.definition: the point in an illness or a story where things must turn better or worse
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或事情发展到必须转好或转坏的关头
senses.example: The fever reached its crisis on the third night.
senses.exampleCN: 高烧在第三天夜里到了紧要关头。
senses.why: An illness also arrives at a fork and must choose a side.
senses.whyCN: 疾病也会走到一个岔口，必须选一边。

senses.title: A lasting hard state
senses.definition: a continuing state of serious difficulty in a society or system
senses.definitionCN: 社会或系统中持续存在的严重困难状态
senses.example: The housing crisis has lasted for years.
senses.exampleCN: 住房困境已经持续多年。
senses.why: Some turning points never quite turn, and become everyday life.
senses.whyCN: 有些转折点始终没转过去，就成了日常。

intro.en: Crisis comes from Greek krisis, a decision, from krinein, to separate or judge.
intro.cn: crisis 源自希腊语 krisis（决断），再往上是 krinein（分开、判断）。

items.en: Krinein meant to separate or to judge.
items.cn: krinein 意为分开或判断。

items.en: Krisis named a decision or a turning point.
items.cn: krisis 指决断或转折点。

items.en: Medical Latin used crisis for the decisive point of an illness.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语用 crisis 指疾病的决定性时刻。

items.en: Crisis entered English first as a medical term.
items.cn: crisis 最初作为医学术语进入英语。

items.en: It spread to politics, money and daily life.
items.cn: 它扩展到政治、金钱与日常生活。

items.en: It now names any dangerous turning point.
items.cn: 今天它指任何危险的转折点。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cri- stem of judging, and the meaning group names other moments of danger.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示判断的 cri- 词干，近义组列出其他危险的时刻。

entries.definition: a person who judges works or actions
entries.definitionCN: 评判作品或行为的人

entries.definition: very serious, or very important
entries.definitionCN: 非常严重或非常关键的

entries.definition: words that judge faults or merits
entries.definitionCN: 评判缺点或优点的话

entries.definition: a sudden dangerous event needing quick action
entries.definitionCN: 需要迅速行动的突发危险事件

entries.definition: a particular point in time or events
entries.definitionCN: 时间或事件中的某个特定节点

entries.definition: a difficult situation hard to escape
entries.definitionCN: 难以脱身的困难处境

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with rising water and end with a fork that never closes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从上涨的水开始，最后落到一个始终没合上的岔口。

normal.en: Crisis and critic share a root: both are about judging.
normal.cn: crisis 与 critic 同根：两者都关乎判断。

normal.en: A crisis is a clock with no spare hours.
normal.cn: 危机是一只没有多余时辰的钟。

normal.en: Two roads open, and neither waits.
normal.cn: 两条路一起打开，谁也不等你。

normal.en: The word sounds like cry, and someone always cries.
normal.cn: 这个词听着像 cry，而总有人在哭。

normal.en: A long crisis is just a turn that never came.
normal.cn: 漫长的危机，只是一个始终没来的转折。

abstract.en: Picture water an inch below the top of a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象水面离墙顶只差一寸。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone looks at one clock.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人都盯着同一只钟。

abstract.en: Picture a road split with no sign at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路分成两岔，却没有路牌。

examples.en: The government acted quickly during the crisis.
examples.cn: 政府在危机期间行动迅速。

examples.en: Two crises hit the company in one year.
examples.cn: 一年之内两场危机击中了这家公司。

examples.en: The illness passed its crisis before dawn.
examples.cn: 病情在天亮前过了危险期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crisis 记成一个必须当场做决定的岔路口：一步走错，后面全变，这就是危机。

root: 源自希腊语 krisis（决断、判断），再往上是 krinein（分开、辨别）；本义是「必须做出决断的那一刻」，由医学上的危险期扩展到政治、经济与生活的转折关头。

sensesIntro.en: From a dangerous moment that demands a decision, to a turning point, to a difficulty that never turns.
sensesIntro.cn: 从必须决断的危险时刻，到转折点，再到始终没转过去的困境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water rising to the top of a dike.
core.cn: 核心意象：水涨到堤坝顶端。

branches.en: Danger grows until a decision can no longer wait.
branches.cn: 危险渐长，直到决断再也不能等。

branches.en: An illness or a story reaches a fork and turns.
branches.cn: 疾病或事情走到岔口，然后转向。

branches.en: When the turn never comes, difficulty becomes normal.
branches.cn: 转折没来时，困难就成了常态。

branches.en: Every crisis is a decision point under pressure.
branches.cn: 每一场危机都是压力下的决断点。

branches.en: Some turning points last so long that they turn into daily life.
branches.cn: 有些转折拖得太久，就变成了日常。

intro.en: Crisis belongs to the Greek family of krinein, to judge, which also gives critic and criterion.
intro.cn: crisis 属于希腊语 krinein（判断）这一族，critic 与 criterion 也出自这里。

latinIntro.en: The Greek stem kri- passed into Latin and English as cri-, the stem of judging.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词干 kri- 经拉丁语进入英语，变成表示判断的 cri-。

items.exampleCN: 这场危机考验了每一位领导者。

items.meaningCN: 非常严重或非常关键的

items.example: The critic praised the new play.
items.exampleCN: 评论家称赞了这部新戏。
这项计划招来尖锐批评。

items.example: They criticize the choice of site.

items.meaning: a careful judgement of a work
in a way that decides the outcome

latinEntries.example: Greek krisis named the moment of decision.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 krisis 指做出决断的时刻。

definition_zh: 目标；目的；瞄准（动作）；瞄准（动词）；旨在；针对
definition_en: a result that a person wants to achieve, or the act of pointing a weapon or camera at something; as a verb, to point at a target or to intend a result
core_image: 弓弦拉满，箭尖压住远处的靶心
scene: 靶场上风很轻，射手把弓举到肩高，眼睛锁住远处的圆心。 She raised the rifle and aimed at the centre of the target.
sceneCN: 这里 aim 是「瞄准」（第 3 个义项：把武器或镜头对准某处）；句意为她举起步枪，瞄准靶心。画面里是靶场、弓与远处的圆心。

pos.zh: 名词：目标；目的；瞄准的动作

collocations.zh: 旨在做某事；力争做某事

derivatives.zh: 由 aim 加形容词后缀 -less 构成，义为「无目标的、漫无目的的」
由 aimless 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「漫无目的地」
由 aimless 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「无目标、漫无目的的状态」

senses.title: A purpose or goal
senses.definition: something that a person hopes to achieve by doing something
senses.definitionCN: 一个人希望通过行动达成的结果
senses.example: Her main aim was to finish the race without stopping.
senses.exampleCN: 她的主要目标是中途不停跑完全程。
senses.why: To shoot straight you must first fix a point to shoot at; pull that point out of the bow and it becomes the goal of any effort.
senses.whyCN: 要把箭射准，先得定一个可射的点；把这个点从弓上抽出来，它就是任何努力想要抵达的「目标」。

senses.title: The act of taking aim
senses.definition: the act of pointing a weapon or camera at a target, especially in the phrase take aim
senses.definitionCN: 把武器或镜头对准目标的行为，尤见于短语 take aim
senses.example: The archer took aim and released the string.
senses.exampleCN: 弓箭手瞄准后松开了弓弦。
senses.why: This is the noun at its most physical: it names the few seconds between raising the weapon and letting it go.
senses.whyCN: 这是名词最实在的一面：它指的是举起武器到放手之间那几秒钟，动作还没结果，只有对准。

senses.title: To point at a target
senses.definition: to point a weapon, camera or device toward a target
senses.definitionCN: 把武器、镜头或装置朝向某个目标
senses.example: He aimed the telescope at the brightest star in the cluster.
senses.exampleCN: 他把望远镜对准星团中最亮的那颗星。
senses.why: The verb spells out the movement the noun implies: the front end of a thing is turned until it lines up with the target.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词暗含的动作摊开：把某物的前端转过去，直到它与目标连成一条直线。

senses.title: To intend to achieve something
senses.definition: to plan or try to achieve a particular result
senses.definitionCN: 计划或力图取得某个特定结果
senses.example: The new course aims to give students practical lab skills.
senses.exampleCN: 这门新课程旨在让学生掌握实用的实验技能。
senses.why: An intention is a target held inside the mind; the action is loosed at it just as an arrow is loosed at a mark.
senses.whyCN: 意图就是立在心里的一枚靶；行动朝它放出去，和箭朝靶心放出去是同一个动作，所以 aim 从「瞄准」转为「旨在」。

senses.title: To direct something at a group
senses.definition: to direct a product, message or action toward a particular group or person
senses.definitionCN: 把产品、讯息或行动对准某一特定群体或个人
senses.example: The campaign is aimed at teenagers who have never voted.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宣传活动面向从未投过票的青少年。
senses.why: Replace the paper target with people: whatever is aimed is now pointed at an audience, and the word means targeting rather than shooting.
senses.whyCN: 把纸靶换成人：被对准的东西现在指向一群受众，于是这个词说的是「针对谁」，而不是「射中什么」。

intro.en: Aim comes from Old French, and behind the French verb stands a Latin verb about judging worth, which is why the word once meant estimate before it meant point.
intro.cn: aim 来自古法语，法语动词背后是一个表示「估量价值」的拉丁动词，因此这个词先有「估量」之意，后才有「对准」之意。

items.en: Aestimare meant 'to value, estimate, judge the worth of something', and it also gave English estimate and esteem.
items.cn: aestimare 意为「估价、估量、判断价值」，它也为英语提供了 estimate 与 esteem。

items.en: Old French aesmer, also written esmer, developed the senses 'to estimate, to guess, to aim'; the exact route from valuing to aiming is generally accepted but the details are debated.
items.cn: 古法语 aesmer（亦写作 esmer）发展出「估量、推测、瞄准」等义；从「估价」到「瞄准」的路径一般认为成立，但具体细节仍有争论。

items.en: The verb entered English in the Middle English period with both the estimating and the pointing senses still alive.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语时期进入英语，「估量」与「对准」两个意思当时都还活着。

items.en: The noun aim is recorded later, from the verb, and settles into the sense of a purpose or a mark to be hit.
items.cn: 名词 aim 出现较晚，由动词而来，逐渐固定为「目的」或「要击中的标记」。

items.en: The purpose sense now dominates in ordinary use, while take aim keeps the old bodily picture of a weapon held steady.
items.cn: 现代英语里「目的」义在日常使用中占主导，而 take aim 仍保留着端稳武器那个身体画面。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin root or the same English stem; the second group holds the nouns and verbs that overlap with aim in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组由同一拉丁词根或同一英语词干构成；第二组是意思与 aim 重叠的名词与动词。

entries.definition: Without a purpose or direction; the -less suffix removes exactly what aim supplies.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无目标的、漫无目的的」，后缀 -less 正好去掉了 aim 所提供的东西。

entries.definition: In a way that shows no purpose, as in walking aimlessly through the streets.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「漫无目的地」，如毫无目标地在街上走。

entries.definition: To judge an amount or value roughly; it shares the Latin root aestimare with aim but kept the valuing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「估计、估算」，与 aim 同出拉丁词根 aestimare，但保留了「估量价值」的意思。

entries.definition: To respect or value highly; another descendant of aestimare, with worth turned into personal regard.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「尊重、敬重」，也是 aestimare 的后代，只是把「价值」转成了对人的看重。

entries.definition: The result a person or team works toward; often a single concrete end, as in a career goal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目标」，常指单一而具体的结果，如职业目标。

entries.definition: A mark to be hit, or a figure to be reached; it keeps more of the physical shooting image than aim does.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「靶子、指标」，比 aim 保留了更多「射击靶标」的实体意象。

entries.definition: The reason why something is done; it explains motive rather than naming the result to be reached.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目的、用意」，解释的是做事的理由，而不是要抵达的结果。

entries.definition: A stated result that an organisation plans to reach; formal and often measurable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目标、指标」，指机构计划达成的明确结果，语气正式，常可量化。

entries.definition: What a person means to do; it stays inside the mind and makes no claim that anything was hit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「意图」，指人打算做什么，停留在心里，并不表示真的击中了什么。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and the phrases in which aim does its daily work.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用的是真实的拉丁词根，以及 aim 日常真正出现的搭配。

normal.en: Aestimare is to judge a distance and a value: an archer estimates before releasing, and that estimate became aim.
normal.cn: aestimare 是估量距离与价值：射手放箭前先估量，这份估量就变成了 aim。

normal.en: Estimate and esteem are cousins: same root, one still counts, one still values.
normal.cn: estimate 与 esteem 是表亲：同一个词根，一个还在数，一个还在看重。

normal.en: Take aim keeps the body in the word: hands steady, eye on the mark.
normal.cn: take aim 把身体留在词里：手要稳，眼要看住标记。

normal.en: Aim at is for a target; aim to is for a plan.
normal.cn: aim at 对着靶子，aim to 对着计划。

normal.en: The -less in aimless simply removes the target and leaves the walking.
normal.cn: aimless 里的 -less 只是拿掉了靶子，留下还在走的人。

abstract.en: Picture a dark room with one lit point on the far wall: everything you do turns until it lines up with that point.
abstract.cn: 想象一间黑屋子，远墙上只有一个亮点：你做的每件事都在转动，直到与那个点连成一线。

abstract.en: The point can be a deer, a star, a market or a child's future; only the distance changes.
abstract.cn: 那个点可以是鹿、星星、市场，也可以是孩子的未来；变的只是距离。

abstract.en: Aim is always a line, never the impact: it stops at the moment of lining up.
abstract.cn: aim 永远是一条线，而不是撞击：它停在「对准」那一刻。

examples.en: Our aim is to cut waste by half this year.
examples.cn: 我们的目标是今年把浪费减少一半。

examples.en: She aimed the camera at the children playing by the river.
examples.cn: 她把相机对准了在河边玩耍的孩子们。

examples.en: The programme aims to help farmers save water.
examples.cn: 这个项目旨在帮助农民节约用水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶姆」——拉弓时轻轻「诶」一声，姆指一松，箭朝目标去了

root: 古法语 aesmer（亦作 esmer）意为「估量、推测、瞄准」，一般认为源自拉丁语 aestimare「估价、判断价值」；由「估量距离」到「对准目标」的语义转移发生在法语阶段，名词 aim 后由动词派生。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses all keep one line: a point is chosen, and something is turned until it lines up with that point, whether the thing is an arrow, a camera, a course or a campaign.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都守着同一条线：先挑定一个点，再把某样东西转到与它连成一线；被转过去的可以是箭、相机、课程，也可以是一场宣传活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawn bow, a steady eye, and a point on the far wall that everything lines up with.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉满的弓、稳住的目光，以及远墙上那个一切都朝它对齐的点。

branches.en: THE RESULT: the point taken out of the bow becomes the goal a person wants to reach.
branches.cn: 结果线：从弓上取下来的那个点，成了人想抵达的目标。

branches.en: THE FEW SECONDS: take aim names the held moment before release, with no result yet.
branches.cn: 瞬间线：take aim 指的是放手之前那段屏住的时间，结果还没发生。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the verb turns the front end of a weapon or lens until it meets the target.
branches.cn: 器物线：动词把武器或镜头的前端转过去，直到与目标相接。

branches.en: THE PLAN: a goal inside the mind is aimed at by a course of action, so pointing becomes intending.
branches.cn: 计划线：心里的目标由一系列行动去对准，于是「瞄准」变成「旨在」。

branches.en: THE AUDIENCE: the paper target is replaced by people, and the line now ends at a group to be reached.
branches.cn: 受众线：纸靶换成人，这条线的终点变成了一群要被触达的人。

intro.en: Aim is a borrowed verb whose Latin root still shows through in estimate and esteem; English builds its own small family on top.
intro.cn: aim 是一个借入的动词，它的拉丁词根仍能从 estimate 与 esteem 看出来；英语在它上面又长出一小族词。

latinIntro.en: Aestimare and its noun aestimatio are recorded Latin; the further origin of the root is source uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: aestimare 及其名词 aestimatio 都是有记录的拉丁语形式；这个词根更早的来源不确定。

items.meaning: to point at, or a goal to reach
items.example: It entered English through Old French.
It survives in estimate and esteem.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根留在 estimate 与 esteem 里。

items.example: It forms misaim, to aim wrongly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 misaim，即瞄错方向。

definition_zh: 使有权；给予资格；给……命名
definition_en: to give someone a right, or to give a title to something
core_image: 一张写着名字的证件，让人有资格走进门内
scene: 公司规定，工作满一年的员工可以享受额外假期。 The company entitles every worker with a year of service to extra holiday.
sceneCN: 这里 entitles 是 entitle 的第三人称单数，表示「使有权享受」（第 1 个义项：赋予某人权利或资格）；句意：公司让工作满一年的员工有权享受额外假期。

pos.zh: 使有权；给予资格；给……命名

derivatives.zh: 权利；应得的份额
有资格的；有权的

senses.title: To give someone a right
senses.definition: to give a person the legal or moral right to have or do something
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某人拥有或做某事的法律或道义权利
senses.example: The law entitles citizens to free medical care.
senses.exampleCN: 法律使公民有权享受免费医疗。
senses.why: En- adds a sense of putting someone into a state, and title supplies the legal claim, so the verb means to grant a right.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 表示使人进入某种状态，title 提供法律主张的含义，所以这个动词表示授予权利。

senses.title: To give a title to a work
senses.definition: to give a name or title to a book, film, song, or other work
senses.definitionCN: 给书、电影、歌曲或其他作品起名称
senses.example: The author entitled her first novel The Long Road.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把她的第一部小说命名为《长路》。
senses.why: Title also means the name of a work, so to entitle is to put a title on it.
senses.whyCN: title 也指作品的名称，因此 entitle 就是给作品加上标题。

senses.title: To give a name or label to a person
senses.definition: to give someone a particular name, label, or description
senses.definitionCN: 给某人一个特定的称呼、标签或描述
senses.example: Critics entitled him the voice of his generation.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称他为那一代人的声音。
senses.why: A title can be an honor or a label, so the verb extends from naming works to naming people.
senses.whyCN: 称号既可以是荣誉也可以是标签，所以这个动词从给作品命名扩展到称呼人。

intro.en: Entitle comes from Latin titulus, a title or label, through Old French entitler, meaning to give a title to.
intro.cn: entitle 来自拉丁语 titulus（标题、称号），经古法语 entitler（给……加标题）进入英语。

items.en: Titulus means a title, label, or inscription.
items.cn: titulus 意为标题、标签或铭文。

items.en: Intitulare means to give a title to something.
items.cn: intitulare 意为给某物加上标题。

items.en: Entitler carries the legal and naming senses.
items.cn: entitler 同时带有法律与命名的含义。

items.en: Entitle means both to name and to give a claim.
items.cn: 中古英语 entitle 既表示命名，也表示赋予权利。

items.en: Modern English keeps the right sense in be entitled to.
items.cn: 现代英语在 be entitled to 中保留「有权」的含义。

note.en: Entitle is a giving word: it gives rights or names, so its company includes title words and words for granting.
note.cn: entitle 是一个「给予」词：给予权利或名称，所以它与 title 词族及表示授予的词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Entitle is en- plus title: to put someone or something into a title, whether a legal claim or a name.
normalIntro.cn: entitle 是 en- 加 title：把人或事物放进一个「名分」里，既可以是法律权利，也可以是名称。

normal.en: A ticket entitles you to a seat, and the verb entitles you to a right.
normal.cn: 一张票让你有座位，动词 entitle 让你有权利。

normal.en: Be entitled to means have the right to.
normal.cn: be entitled to 表示有权享有。

normal.en: A book is entitled, and so is a film.
normal.cn: 书可以被命名，电影也可以。

normal.en: The noun entitlement names the right itself.
normal.cn: 名词 entitlement 指权利本身。

normal.en: Compare title: title is the name, entitle is the act of giving it.
normal.cn: 对比 title：title 是名称，entitle 是给予名称的动作。

abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙被放进一双等待的手中。

abstract.en: Imagine a label being tied to a new book.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标签被系在一本新书上。

abstract.en: Think of a name written at the top of a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被写在页面顶端。

examples.en: This pass entitles you to enter the gallery.
examples.cn: 这张通行证使你有权进入画廊。

examples.en: She entitled her essay A Quiet Morning.
examples.cn: 她把自己的文章命名为《安静的早晨》。

examples.en: The ticket entitles each visitor to one free drink.
examples.cn: 这张票让每位参观者有权获得一杯免费饮料。

root: 拉丁语 titulus（标题、称号）→ 拉丁语 intitulare（加标题）→ 古法语 entitler → 中古英语 entitle，核心义「给予名分」，引申为赋予权利。

sensesIntro.en: Entitle moves from granting a legal claim to giving a work a title, and then to giving a person a label.
sensesIntro.cn: entitle 从授予法律权利，扩展到给作品加标题，再扩展到给人加称号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a document with a name on it that opens a door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写有名字、可以打开一扇门的文书。

branches.en: Granting a right is the dominant legal sense.
branches.cn: 授予权利，是主要的法律义项。

branches.en: Giving a work its name keeps the original title idea.
branches.cn: 给作品命名，保留最初的「标题」概念。

branches.en: Giving a person a label extends naming to people.
branches.cn: 给人加称号，把命名扩展到人。

branches.en: Both rights and titles are things formally granted.

branches.en: A person can be legally entitled and publicly entitled.
branches.cn: 一个人可以依法有权，也可以被公开称呼。

definition_zh: 结合；联合；兼有；联合收割机
definition_en: to join two or more things so that they work or exist together, or to have two qualities at the same time
core_image: 两股溪流在山脚汇成一条更宽的河
scene: 两支小队伍把各自的工具摆到一处，合力搭起一座桥。 They combined their tools and built the bridge in a day.

senses.title: To join two things
senses.definition: to put two or more things together so that they form one whole
senses.definitionCN: 把两样或更多事物放在一起，使它们成为一个整体
senses.example: Combine the flour and the sugar in a large bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 把面粉和糖放进一个大碗里拌匀。
senses.why: The oldest sense is physical: two things are brought into one place.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是具体的：把两样东西带到同一个地方。

senses.title: To have two qualities
senses.definition: to have two different qualities or roles at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 同时具备两种不同的性质或身份
senses.example: Her job combines teaching with research.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作兼有教学与研究。
senses.why: When two roles meet in one person, they are combined rather than mixed.
senses.whyCN: 两种身份集中在一个人身上，是结合而非混杂。

senses.title: A harvesting machine
senses.definition: a large farm machine that cuts and cleans grain in one pass
senses.definitionCN: 一次完成收割与脱粒的大型农业机械
senses.example: The combine moved slowly across the wheat field.
senses.exampleCN: 联合收割机缓缓驶过麦田。
senses.why: The machine does several farm jobs at once, so it is named after combining.
senses.whyCN: 这台机器一次完成好几道农活，因此以「联合」命名。

intro.en: Combine goes back to Latin combinare, a word for joining two things into one.
intro.cn: combine 上溯到拉丁语 combinare，意为把两样东西并成一体。

items.en: Combinare built on com-, together, and bini, two each.
items.cn: combinare 由表示一起的 com- 与表示各两个的 bini 构成。

items.en: Scribes used combinare for uniting separate things.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语文献用 combinare 表示把分开的事物联合起来。

items.en: Old French combiner kept the same practical sense.
items.cn: 古法语 combiner 保留了同样务实的含义。

items.en: English combine entered use for joining forces or ideas.
items.cn: 英语 combine 开始用于联合力量或想法。

items.en: Farmers gave the name combine to a machine that harvests and threshes.
items.cn: 农人把收割与脱粒一体的机器称作 combine。

branches.en: Two roles in one person are joined rather than mixed.

definition_en: relating to law, allowed or required by law, valid in law, connected with the legal profession, or allowed by the rules of a game

scene: 律所的会议室里，律师把合同翻到签字页。 She pointed out that the clause was not legal in this country and had to be rewritten before anyone could sign.
sceneCN: 这里 legal 是「合法的、法律允许的」（第 2 个义项：为法律所允许）；句意：她指出这一条在本国不合法，必须改写之后才能签字。图中可辨识物件：会议室长桌、合同、签字页、法典、印章。

senses.title: Relating to law in general
senses.definition: connected with the law, the courts, or the system of rules a society enforces
senses.definitionCN: 与法律、法院或社会所执行的规则体系有关的
senses.example: She is studying the legal systems of two countries.
senses.exampleCN: 她在研究两个国家的法律体系。
senses.why: Legal began as the adjective of Latin lex 'law', so its widest sense simply marks anything belonging to the law as an institution.
senses.whyCN: legal 最初是拉丁语 lex“法”的形容词，因此最宽的义项只是标记“属于法律这个制度”的事物。

senses.title: Allowed by law
senses.definition: permitted by law; not forbidden or criminal
senses.definitionCN: 为法律所允许的；未被禁止或不算犯罪的
senses.example: In some states it is legal to record a call you take part in.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些州，录下自己参与的通话是合法的。
senses.why: From 'belonging to law' comes 'consistent with law'. The question is no longer what law is about, but whether an act falls inside the permitted line.
senses.whyCN: 从“属于法律”引申出“符合法律”。问题不再是“法管什么”，而是一个行为是否落在被允许的界线之内。

senses.title: Required by law
senses.definition: required or prescribed by law, so that not doing it is a breach
senses.definitionCN: 由法律要求或规定的，不做即构成违法或违约
senses.example: Employers have a legal duty to provide safety training.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主有提供安全培训的法定义务。
senses.why: The same boundary has a second side: what law permits it also commands. A legal duty is not optional, and the adjective shifts from permission to obligation.
senses.whyCN: 同一条界线还有另一面：法律允许的东西，也可以被法律命令。legal duty 不是可选项，形容词于是从“许可”滑向“义务”。

senses.title: Valid and enforceable in law
senses.definition: recognized as valid and enforceable by law, especially of a document, contract or claim
senses.definitionCN: 被法律认可为有效且可执行的，尤指文件、合同或主张
senses.example: The contract is not legal without both signatures.
senses.exampleCN: 没有双方签字，这份合同在法律上不生效。
senses.why: Here legal does not mean 'allowed' but 'having legal force'. A document can be legally made yet legally ineffective if a formality is missing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 legal 不是“被允许”，而是“具有法律效力”。一份文件可以依法制作，却因缺少形式要件而在法律上无效。

senses.title: Of the legal profession
senses.definition: relating to lawyers, their training, or the business of giving legal advice
senses.definitionCN: 与律师、其训练或提供法律意见的业务有关的
senses.example: He left banking for a legal career at thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 他三十岁时离开银行业，转做法律职业。
senses.why: The institution is also a trade. Legal then describes the people and practices that operate the system, not the rules themselves.
senses.whyCN: 法律这套制度同时也是一门行业。legal 于是描述运作这套制度的人与业务，而不是规则本身。

senses.title: Relating to lawsuits
senses.definition: relating to court proceedings or to action taken through the courts
senses.definitionCN: 与法院程序或通过法院采取的行动有关的
senses.example: The tenants threatened legal action over the mould.
senses.exampleCN: 租户因霉斑问题威胁要采取法律诉讼。
senses.why: One branch of the system is dispute. Legal action names the step from a private quarrel to a case that a court can decide.
senses.whyCN: 这套制度的一支是争端。legal action 标记了从私人纠纷跨到“法院可以裁决的案件”的那一步。

senses.title: According to the letter of the law
senses.definition: existing or holding a status in law, even if the actual situation is different
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上存在或拥有某种身份，即使实际情况不同
senses.example: She is the legal owner, though her brother runs the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 她是法律上的所有者，尽管农场由她哥哥经营。
senses.why: Law can assign a name that reality does not match. Legal owner, legal parent and legal fiction all use the adjective to mark the official version, as opposed to the factual one.
senses.whyCN: 法律可以给出一个与现实不符的名义。legal owner、legal parent、legal fiction 都用这个形容词标记“官方版本”，以区别于事实版本。

senses.title: Allowed by the rules of a game
senses.definition: allowed by the rules of a sport or game, though not necessarily by statute
senses.definitionCN: 为运动或游戏规则所允许的，而不一定涉及成文法
senses.example: The tackle was hard but legal.
senses.exampleCN: 那次擒抱很凶，但符合规则。
senses.why: The boundary image is borrowed from law: a game has its own code, and a move inside it is called legal by analogy. Here no court is involved.
senses.whyCN: 这里借用了“界线”的意象：游戏有自己的规则法典，规则内的动作被类比地称为 legal，此时并不涉及法院。

senses.title: Legal-size paper
senses.definition: a US paper size of 8.5 by 14 inches, sold as legal pads and used for long documents
senses.definitionCN: 美国一种 8.5×14 英寸的纸张规格，做成黄色横线稿纸，用于较长的文书
senses.example: He drafted the will on a yellow legal pad.
senses.exampleCN: 他在黄色法定尺寸稿纸上起草了遗嘱。
senses.why: The adjective became a fixed label for a paper size once associated with legal records. This is an attributive use, not a new legal concept.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词固定成了纸张规格的标签，因为这种尺寸曾与法律文书相关。这是定语用法，并不是新的法律概念。

intro.en: Legal is a direct Latin borrowing, not a French one: English took legalis from Latin in the 15c, while loyal came through French from the same source. Its noun is lex, not legare and not licere.
intro.cn: legal 是直接借自拉丁语，而非借自法语：英语在 15 世纪直接取用 legalis；loyal 则是同一来源经法语变来的。它的名词是 lex，不是 legare，也不是 licere。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'of or pertaining to law'. It was borrowed straight from Latin legalis rather than through French.
items.cn: 最早记录于 15 世纪中期的英语，意为“与法律有关的”。它是直接从拉丁语 legalis 借入的，而不是经法语转手。

items.en: legalis 'of or belonging to the law' is formed from lex (genitive legis) 'law, statute, bill' plus -alis 'relating to'.
items.cn: legalis“属于法律的”由 lex（属格 legis）“法、法规、议案”加 -alis“与……有关的”构成。

items.en: lex is traced to PIE *leg- 'to collect, gather'. The idea may be 'that which is collected or laid down', but this semantic step is generally accepted, not documented.
items.cn: lex 被追溯到原始印欧语 *leg-“收集、采集”。其理据可能是“被收集、被放下之物”，但这一步只是一般认为是，并无文献确证。

items.en: legare 'to send, depute; bequeath' is a different verb, source of legate, legacy and allegation. Its connection with lex is source uncertain, so legal must not be treated as derived from legare.
items.cn: legare“派出、委任；遗赠”是另一个动词，是 legate、legacy、allegation 的来源。它与 lex 的联系来源不确定，因此不能把 legal 当作 legare 的派生词。

items.en: licere 'to be permitted' is a third root, the source of license. Being permitted by someone is not the same as being lawful under a statute.
items.cn: licere“被允许”是第三条词根线，是 license 的来源。被某人允许，与在成文法下合法，并不是同一件事。

items.en: Legal now covers the system, permission, obligation, validity and the profession. Loyal, legate and legacy are close relatives in form but come by different routes, so their meanings must not be merged.
items.cn: 现代 legal 覆盖法律体系、许可、义务、效力和法律职业。loyal、legate、legacy 在形式上亲近，却走了不同路线，词义不可合并。

note.en: The look-alike group mixes three neighbours: one from legere 'read', one genuinely from lex, and one from legare 'bequeath'. The near-meaning group separates permission, justification, statute and the courts.
note.cn: 形近组混入三个邻居：一个出自 legere“读”，一个确实出自 lex，一个出自 legare“遗赠”。近义组则把许可、正当性、成文法与法院区分开。

entries.definition: clear enough to read. It looks like legal but comes from legere 'to read', so it has nothing to do with law.
entries.definitionCN: 字迹清楚可读的。它形似 legal，却出自 legere“读”，与法律无关。

entries.definition: lawful or valid; also reasonable and justified. It comes from Latin legitimus, built on lex, so it is a true cousin of legal.
entries.definitionCN: 合法的、有效的；也指合情合理的。它来自以 lex 构成的拉丁语 legitimus，是 legal 真正的同族词。

entries.definition: money or property left to someone by a will. It looks legal, but it comes from legare 'bequeath', not from lex 'law'.
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱留给某人的钱财或财产。它形似 legal，却出自 legare“遗赠”，而非 lex“法”。

entries.definition: allowed by law; not against the law. It is plainer and older than legal and often carries a moral tone that legal lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 法律允许的；不违法的。它比 legal 更朴素、更古老，常带有 legal 所缺的道德意味。

entries.definition: valid according to law or reason. Unlike legal, it can also mean 'fair and justified' outside any statute.
entries.definitionCN: 依法律或依理性有效的。与 legal 不同，它还可以指任何法规之外的事情“合理、正当”。

entries.definition: required or created by a written statute. It is narrower and more technical than legal, which covers the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 由成文法规定或创设的。它比 legal 更窄、更技术化，因为 legal 覆盖整个法律体系。

entries.definition: relating to courts, judges, or the administration of justice. It names one branch of the system, not law as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 与法院、法官或司法有关的。它指体系中的一个分支，而不是整个法律。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: lex (genitive legis) 'law' + -alis, with legitimate, legislature and loyal in the same family. Watch the false friends legere 'read' and legare 'bequeath'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：lex（属格 legis）“法”+ -alis，同族有 legitimate、legislature、loyal。要警惕形近假朋友 legere“读”与 legare“遗赠”。

normal.en: lex, legis is the noun 'law'; legalis adds -alis 'relating to'. The core is simply 'of the law'.
normal.cn: lex、legis 是名词“法”；legalis 加上 -alis“与……有关”。核心意思就是“属于法的”。

normal.en: legitimate and legislature are built on the same lex, which is why they all carry a law meaning.
normal.cn: legitimate 与 legislature 都建在同一个 lex 上，所以它们都带“法”的含义。

normal.en: legacy comes from legare 'bequeath', not from lex. A legacy is what a will leaves, not what a statute says.
normal.cn: legacy 出自 legare“遗赠”，不是 lex。legacy 是遗嘱留下的东西，不是法规规定的条文。

normal.en: loyal is legalis after its trip through French: same source, different word. Loyalty is faithfulness, not legality.
normal.cn: loyal 是 legalis 经法语旅行后的样子：同源而异词。loyalty 是忠诚，不是合法性。

normal.en: legal age and legal duty show the two sides of the boundary: one permits, the other obliges.
normal.cn: legal age 与 legal duty 展示同一条界线的两面：一面是允许，一面是强制。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on a floor: inside it, everything is allowed; on the line, everything is required; outside it, nothing is recognized. Legal is the line itself, seen from any side.
abstract.cn: 想象地板上画的一条线：线内一切被允许，线上一切被要求，线外一切不被承认。legal 就是这条线本身，从哪一面看都算。

abstract.en: The same stamp can mean 'you may', 'you must' or 'this counts', depending on which document it lands on.
abstract.cn: 同一枚印章落在不同文件上，可以表示“你可以”“你必须”或“这份算数”。

abstract.en: Law has a name for things that do not exist in fact: the legal owner is a person the paper sees, not always the person the field sees.
abstract.cn: 法律会为事实上不存在的东西命名：法律上的所有者是纸面看见的人，未必是田里看见的人。

examples.en: The company sought legal advice before signing the deal.
examples.cn: 公司在签署交易前寻求法律咨询。

examples.en: Is it legal to park here after six?
examples.cn: 六点以后在这里停车合法吗？

examples.en: She was the legal owner of the flat but had never lived in it.
examples.cn: 她是这套公寓法律上的所有者，却从未住过。

dict_mnemonic.text: “李哥”——李哥办事只走正规手续 → legal 合法的、法律的

root: 拉丁语 lex（属格 legis）“法”+ -alis“与……有关的”，核心是“写在法典里、有法律依据”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of legal, all radiating from one noun, lex. A thing can belong to the law, be allowed by it, be required by it, be valid under it, be done by its professionals, or merely carry its label.
sensesIntro.cn: legal 的九个义项都从一个名词 lex 放射出来：某事物可以属于法律、被法律允许、被法律要求、在法律上有效、由法律从业者去做，或只是贴着法律的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line written into a code, marking what is allowed, required and recognized.
core.cn: 核心意象：写进法典的一条界线，标出什么被允许、什么被要求、什么被承认。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND PROFESSION: law as an institution, and the people who operate it.
branches.cn: 体系与职业：作为制度的法律，以及运作它的人。

branches.en: PERMISSION: what statute allows, and, by analogy, what the rules of a game allow.
branches.cn: 许可：成文法允许的事，以及类比到游戏规则所允许的事。

branches.en: OBLIGATION: the other side of the boundary, where the law commands rather than permits.
branches.cn: 义务：界线的另一面，法律在这里不是允许而是命令。

branches.en: LEGAL EFFECT: validity, court action, and the official status that may differ from fact.
branches.cn: 法律效力：有效性、诉讼，以及可能与事实不同的官方身份。

branches.en: PAPER SIZE: a fixed attributive use, where the adjective labels a format rather than a legal idea.
branches.cn: 纸张规格：固定的定语用法，形容词在这里标记的是尺寸，而不是法律概念。

intro.en: Legal is a Latin adjective borrowed whole. English adds -ly for the adverb, -ity for the abstract noun, -ize for the verb, and the negative prefix il- before l.
intro.cn: legal 是整体借入的拉丁形容词。英语加 -ly 构成副词，-ity 构成抽象名词，-ize 构成动词，并在 l 前用否定前缀 il-。

latinIntro.en: The lex family is wide: legitimate, legislature, loyal and privilege all contain the law noun in different shapes. Keep it apart from legere 'read' and legare 'bequeath'.
latinIntro.cn: lex 词族很宽：legitimate、legislature、loyal、privilege 都以不同形态含有“法”这个名词。要把它与 legere“读”、legare“遗赠”分开。

items.meaning: in a way that is allowed by law; according to law
items.meaningCN: 合法地；在法律上（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 那场抗议是合法举行的。

items.meaning: the quality or state of being legal
items.meaningCN: 合法性（-ity 构成抽象名词）
items.example: The court questioned the legality of the search.
items.exampleCN: 法院质疑那次搜查的合法性。

items.meaning: to make something legal by law
items.example: Several states have legalized recreational use.
items.exampleCN: 有几个州已将娱乐性使用合法化。

items.meaningCN: 非法的；违法的（il- 是否定前缀，用在 l 前）
items.example: It is illegal to dump waste in the river.
items.exampleCN: 向河里倾倒废物是违法的。

items.example: The noun supplies the law at the centre of legal.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供 legal 核心的“法”。

items.example: The stem appears in legal, legislate and legitimate.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 legal、legislate 与 legitimate。

items.example: It turns the noun for law into the adjective legal.
items.exampleCN: 它把“法”这个名词变成形容词 legal。

items.meaning: the quality or state of being
items.example: It forms legality, the quality of being lawful.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 legality，即合乎法律的性质。

items.meaning: strict adherence to law or to written rules
items.meaningCN: 条文主义；死守法律条文
items.example: Critics say legalism ignores the purpose behind the rule.
items.exampleCN: 批评者说条文主义忽视了规则背后的目的。

latinEntries.meaning: lawful, valid; also reasonable and justified
latinEntries.meaningCN: 合法的、有效的；也指合理正当的（词根仍是 lex“法”）

latinEntries.meaning: the body that has power to make laws
latinEntries.meaningCN: 立法机关（legis 属格 + lator“提出者”）

latinEntries.meaning: faithful to a ruler, country or promise
latinEntries.meaningCN: 忠诚的；同源于 legalis，经法语音变而成，不是英语 legal 的派生

latinEntries.meaning: a special right; originally a law made for an individual
latinEntries.meaningCN: 特权；原指为某个人制定的法律（privus“个人”+ lex“法”）

definition_zh: 连接；联系；关系；转乘衔接；人脉
definition_en: the state of being joined, a relationship, or a transport link that lets you continue a journey
core_image: 一张网把散落的点一格一格连起来
scene: 火车晚点，年轻人冲上月台时车门刚好关上。 I missed the connection by two minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 connection 指「转乘衔接」（第 3 个义项：交通工具之间的接续）；句意是我差两分钟没赶上换乘。

derivatives.zh: 连接；联系；接通
连接的；起连接作用的
相连的；有关系的
连接器；接头

senses.title: Being joined
senses.definition: the state of two things being joined together
senses.definitionCN: 两件东西被接在一起的状态
senses.example: Check the connection between the pipe and the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 检查一下管道和水箱之间的连接。
senses.why: Two parts stop being separate once a joint holds them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了接头把两部分固定住，它们就不再彼此分开。

senses.title: A relationship
senses.definition: a relationship between people, things or ideas, including people you know
senses.definitionCN: 人、事物或想法之间的关系，也包括认识的人
senses.example: There is a clear connection between smoking and heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟与心脏病之间有明显的联系。
senses.why: A link that cannot be seen still pulls two facts toward each other.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的联系，仍然会把两件事实拉在一起。

senses.title: A travel link
senses.definition: a bus, train or flight that lets you continue a journey
senses.definitionCN: 让你继续行程的接驳车、火车或航班
senses.example: The flight was late, so I missed my connection.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机晚点，所以我错过了转乘。
senses.why: One vehicle hands you to another, and the journey stays unbroken.
senses.whyCN: 一个交通工具把你交给另一个，行程因此不断。

intro.en: Connection comes from Latin connexio, a binding together, from connectere, to tie, and was spelled with an x for centuries.
intro.cn: connection 来自拉丁语 connexio，意为绑在一起，源自动词 connectere（系绑），有几个世纪都写作 x 的拼法。

items.en: Nectere meant to tie, and connectere meant to tie together.
items.cn: nectere 意为系绑，connectere 意为绑在一起。

items.en: Connexio named the joint or the act of binding.
items.cn: connexio 指接合处或绑缚的行为。

items.en: Old French connexion kept the x of the Latin participle.
items.cn: 古法语 connexion 保留了拉丁语分词里的 x。

items.en: English took the word as connexion and used it for any join.
items.cn: 英语以 connexion 的形式借入，用来指任何连接。

items.en: Writers began to spell it connection to match the Latin verb.
items.cn: 写作者开始把它拼作 connection，以贴合拉丁动词。

items.en: Connection is now standard, and it also means a train or flight link.
items.cn: 如今 connection 是标准拼法，也指火车或航班的接续。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that echo the sound or shape of connection, and the meaning group names other kinds of link.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 connection 音形相近的词，近义组列出其他表示联系的说法。

entries.definition: the older British spelling of connection
entries.definitionCN: connection 的旧式英式拼法

entries.definition: a change that makes something right
entries.definitionCN: 改正；修正

entries.definition: a group of things gathered together
entries.definitionCN: 收藏品；收集

entries.definition: a relationship or a joining part
entries.definitionCN: 联系；环节

entries.definition: the way two people or things are connected
entries.definitionCN: 关系；关联

entries.definition: a strong tie between people
entries.definitionCN: 纽带；情感联系

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two dots joined by a line, then move to people who know each other and to two trains meeting on a platform.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个被一条线连起来的点开始，再到彼此认识的人，最后到月台上相接的两趟列车。

normal.en: Con- is together, nect- is bind, and -ion makes it a thing, so a connection is a binding.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，nect- 是绑，-ion 把它变成名词，所以 connection 就是一次绑缚。

normal.en: Two dots and one line: that is the whole picture.
normal.cn: 两个点加一条线，整幅画面就是这些。

normal.en: A bad connection makes a voice break into pieces.
normal.cn: 连接不好时，说话声会碎成一片片。

normal.en: Some connections are people: a friend who knows a friend.
normal.cn: 有些 connection 指的是人：朋友的朋友。

normal.en: A missed connection leaves you standing while the train leaves.
normal.cn: 错过转乘，就只能站着看火车开走。

abstract.en: Picture two islands with one rope stretched between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两座岛之间拉着一根绳。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake that lasts a whole career.
abstract.cn: 想象一次握手支撑起整个职业生涯。

abstract.en: Picture a platform clock showing the same minute twice.
abstract.cn: 想象站台时钟两次指到同一分钟。

examples.en: The connection between diet and mood is well known.
examples.cn: 饮食与情绪之间的联系广为人知。

examples.en: He has good connections in the publishing world.
examples.cn: 他在出版界有很好的人脉。

examples.en: I have a connection in Paris, so the trip takes two flights.
examples.cn: 我要在巴黎转机，所以这趟行程要坐两班飞机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 connection 记成 con（一起）加 nect（绑）加 ion（名词）：绑在一起的结果，就是连接，也可以指人与人之间的门路。

root: 源自拉丁语 connexio（com 一起 + nectere 系绑），本义是绑在一起，后引申为联系、关系、人脉与交通接续。

sensesIntro.en: From a physical joint, to a relationship between facts or people, and finally to a train or flight that carries you onward.
sensesIntro.cn: 从物理上的接头，到事实或人之间的关系，最后到把你继续送走的火车或航班。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two points apart, joined by one taut line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个分开的点，被一条绷紧的线连起来。

branches.en: The basic sense is a joint where two parts hold together.
branches.cn: 基本义项是两部分相互固定的接头。

branches.en: The link can be invisible yet still tie facts or people.
branches.cn: 这种联系可以看不见，却仍然把事实或人系在一起。

branches.en: In travel, the link is a vehicle that takes over from another.
branches.cn: 在旅途中，这一环是从另一班接手的交通工具。

branches.en: Both a wire and a friendship need two ends that stay in place.
branches.cn: 电线与友情都需要两端各自守在原处。

branches.en: A good contact at an airport is a personal connection and a flight link at once.
branches.cn: 机场里的熟人，同时是人脉与航班接续。

intro.en: Connection is built on Latin com-, together, plus nectere, to bind, with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: connection 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 nectere（系绑）加上名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin bind base nect- also appears in nexus and annex, and its participle gave the x spelling connexio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的系绑词基 nect- 也出现在 nexus 与 annex 中，其分词形式带来了 connexio 的 x 拼法。

items.meaning: the state or act of being joined
items.exampleCN: 这个接头在压力下没有松脱。
结缔组织支撑着这个器官。

items.meaning: a piece that links two devices

items.exampleCN: 这些事件彼此密切相关。

items.meaning: the same word in its older British form
items.meaningCN: 同一个词的旧式英式写法

items.example: The station is a nexus of the city.
items.exampleCN: 这座车站是城市的枢纽。

definition_zh: 胜利；获胜；成功
definition_en: success in a contest, battle, or struggle against an opponent or a difficulty
core_image: 终场哨响，全队抱在一起跳起来
scene: 决赛最后一分钟，主队攻入一球，看台上的人全都站了起来。 The home side celebrated a narrow victory over the champions.
sceneCN: 这里 victory 是「胜利」（第 1 个义项：在比赛、战斗或与对手、困难的较量中取得胜利）；句意为主队在主场以微弱优势战胜了冠军队。终场哨响时抱在一起的人就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ious 构成，义为「胜利的；获胜的」
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「胜利地」
同源名词，义为「胜利者」

senses.title: Success in a contest or battle
senses.definition: the act of defeating an opponent in a game, fight, or war
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、战斗或战争中击败对手
senses.example: The home side celebrated a narrow victory over the champions.
senses.exampleCN: 主队庆祝以微弱优势战胜了冠军队。
senses.why: Latin victoria came from victor, the winner, and a winner is what a contest produces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 victoria 来自 victor（胜者），而胜者正是竞争产生的结果。

senses.title: Success in a struggle against difficulty
senses.definition: success in overcoming a problem, illness, or obstacle
senses.definitionCN: 克服问题、疾病或障碍而取得成功
senses.example: Her recovery was a quiet victory over fear.
senses.exampleCN: 她的康复是一场无声的、战胜恐惧的胜利。
senses.why: The opponent need not be a person: a disease or a fear can be beaten too.
senses.whyCN: 对手不必是人：疾病、恐惧同样可以被战胜。

senses.title: An advantage gained for a cause
senses.definition: a result that proves right or helps a principle or group
senses.definitionCN: 证明某一主张正确、或有利于某一原则与群体的结果
senses.example: The ruling is a victory for press freedom.
senses.exampleCN: 这一裁定是新闻自由的胜利。
senses.why: When a court or an election settles a principle, the side that principle favours has won.
senses.whyCN: 当法院或选举就某原则定论时，该原则所支持的一方就等于获胜。

senses.title: In ancient use, the goddess of success
senses.definition: the Roman goddess who personified success
senses.definitionCN: 古罗马象征成功的女神维多利亚
senses.example: A statue of Victory stood at the head of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅一端立着一尊胜利女神像。
senses.why: Rome turned abstract success into a goddess, and her name is this noun.
senses.whyCN: 古罗马把抽象的成功人格化为女神，女神的名称正是这个词。

senses.title: The moment of triumph in speech or writing
senses.definition: a report or celebration of a win, as in headlines
senses.definitionCN: 对胜利的报道或庆祝，如新闻标题中的用法
senses.example: News of the victory reached the capital by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 胜利的消息中午就传到了首都。
senses.why: Once news travels, the abstract win becomes a piece of news people pass on.
senses.whyCN: 消息一旦传开，抽象的胜利就成了一条被人们转述的新闻。

intro.en: Victory goes back to Latin victoria, from victor, the one who wins.
intro.cn: victory 追溯至拉丁语 victoria，来自 victor（胜者）。

items.en: Vincere meant to conquer, and victor named the one who conquered.
items.cn: vincere 意为征服，victor 指征服者。

items.en: Victoria was the abstract noun for the win itself, and also a goddess.
items.cn: victoria 既是「胜利」这一抽象名词，也是一位女神。

items.en: French victoire carried the word toward English.
items.cn: 法语 victoire 把该词带向英语。

items.en: English took victory for a win in battle or in argument.
items.cn: 中世纪英语以 victory 指战斗或辩论中的胜利。

items.en: Sport and politics widened it to games, elections, and moral causes.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到比赛、选举与道义主张。

note.en: The first group holds the victor family, the second the close words for winning and losing.
note.cn: 第一组是 victor 词族，第二组是表示胜负的相近词。

entries.definition: the one who wins
entries.definitionCN: 胜利者

entries.definition: having won
entries.definitionCN: 胜利的

entries.definition: in a winning way
entries.definitionCN: 胜利地

entries.definition: to make someone a victim
entries.definitionCN: 使受害

entries.definition: a great and public win
entries.definitionCN: 凯旋；大捷

entries.definition: the reaching of a goal
entries.definitionCN: 成功

entries.definition: the taking of land by force
entries.definitionCN: 征服

entries.definition: a loss to an opponent
entries.definitionCN: 失败；击败

normalIntro.en: From the Latin goddess of success to the final score of a match: victory always ends a contest.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁语的成功女神到比赛的最终比分：victory 总在为一场较量收尾。

normal.en: Victory and victim look alike but have no common Latin root.
normal.cn: victory 与 victim 形似，却没有共同的拉丁词根。

normal.en: Drop the -y and add -or for victor, the winner.
normal.cn: 去掉 -y 加 -or 即 victor，获胜的人。

normal.en: Victorious adds -ious, like glorious.
normal.cn: victorious 加 -ious，如同 glorious。

normal.en: The plural changes y to ies: victories.
normal.cn: 复数 y 变 ies：victories。

normal.en: V is the sign of the Roman victory goddess on coins.
normal.cn: 古罗马钱币上的 V 就是胜利女神的标记。

abstract.en: See the scoreboard freeze at one goal ahead.
abstract.cn: 想记分牌定格在领先一球。

abstract.en: Hear a whole stand breathe out at the final whistle.
abstract.cn: 听终场哨响时整片看台一起呼气。

abstract.en: Picture a stone goddess with wings at the hall door.
abstract.cn: 想大厅门口一尊带翅膀的石女神。

examples.en: The team has now won three victories in a row.
examples.cn: 这支队伍如今已连赢三场。

examples.en: The law was seen as a victory for small farmers.
examples.cn: 这项法律被视为小农的胜利。

examples.en: They claimed victory before all the votes were counted.
examples.cn: 票还没数完他们就宣布获胜了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克多利」——维克多力气最大，比赛拿了第一，胜利归他。

root: 拉丁语 vincere（征服）→ victor（胜者）→ victoria（胜利）→ 法语 victoire → 英语 victory

sensesIntro.en: One noun runs from a battle won, through a fear overcome and a principle upheld, to a goddess and a headline.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词从打赢一场仗，延伸到战胜恐惧、捍卫原则，再延伸到女神与新闻标题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a team leaping together as the whistle blows.
core.cn: 核心意象：终场哨响时全队一起跃起。

branches.en: The match branch: a narrow win at home.
branches.cn: 比赛分支：主场的险胜。

branches.en: The illness branch: a quiet win over fear.
branches.cn: 疾病分支：战胜恐惧的无声胜利。

branches.en: The cause branch: a ruling for press freedom.
branches.cn: 主张分支：有利于新闻自由的裁定。

branches.en: The altar branch: the winged goddess on her pedestal.
branches.cn: 神坛分支：柱座上的带翅膀女神。

branches.en: The news branch: word of the win reaching the capital.
branches.cn: 新闻分支：捷报传至首都。

intro.en: The root vinc-, vict- means to conquer; -or, -ory, and -ious build the family.
intro.cn: 词根 vinc-、vict- 意为征服，-or、-ory、-ious 构成这个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vincere gave victor and victoria; the stem vict- carries the sense of overcoming into every English form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vincere 派生 victor 与 victoria，词干 vict- 把「克服」之义带进每个英语形式。

items.example: Vict- carries the sense of winning.
A victor is the one who wins.
Victory names the state of having won.
items.exampleCN: victory 指已经获胜的状态。

items.example: Victorious means full of the win.
items.exampleCN: victorious 意为充满胜利感的。

items.example: They marched victoriously into the square.

items.exampleCN: 这个赛季带来六场胜利。

items.example: The triumph was marked by a parade.
items.exampleCN: 以游行的方式庆祝这次凯旋。

items.example: Defeat taught them more than victory.
items.exampleCN: 失败教会他们的比胜利更多。

definition_zh: 凌乱的；脏乱的；难清理的；棘手的；混乱的
definition_en: untidy, dirty or full of disorder; difficult to deal with or unpleasant because it involves confusion, trouble or unpleasant details
core_image: 散场后的儿童房：积木铺满地板，画纸和蜡笔摊在床上，门边还倒着一杯果汁
scene: 孩子们跑出去玩了，地板上积木铺了一地，床上的画纸和蜡笔也没人收，门边还倒着一杯果汁。 The children's room is terribly messy after they played all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里是「凌乱的、脏乱的」（第 1 个义项：东西没归位的状态）；句意为孩子们玩了一下午后，房间乱得不像话。图中可辨识物件：铺满地板的积木、摊在床上的画纸与蜡笔、门边倒着的果汁杯。

pos.zh: 凌乱的；脏乱的；棘手的；混乱的

collocations.zh: 一场闹得很难看的离婚

derivatives.zh: messy 的基础词，义为「混乱；脏乱；污物」，也可作动词「弄乱；搞砸」
由 messy 去 y 加 -ily 构成，义为「凌乱地；杂乱地」
由 messy 去 y 加 -ness 构成，义为「凌乱；杂乱的性质」

senses.title: Untidy or dirty
senses.definition: not neat or clean, with things left in the wrong places or dirt spread around
senses.definitionCN: 不整洁不干净，东西没放回原位，或者脏东西摊得到处都是
senses.example: The children's room is terribly messy after they played all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们玩了一下午之后，他们的房间乱得不像话。
senses.why: Messy is mess plus the suffix -y, so the adjective literally means full of mess: whatever the noun mess covers, the adjective describes.
senses.whyCN: messy 就是 mess 加上后缀 -y，字面意思是「充满 mess」：名词 mess 指什么，形容词就形容什么。

senses.title: Producing or involving dirt
senses.titleCN: 弄得脏兮兮的；难收拾的
senses.definition: likely to make things dirty, or unpleasant to touch or eat because it spreads or drips
senses.definitionCN: 容易把东西弄脏的，或因流淌滴洒而摸起来、吃起来令人不快的
senses.example: Spaghetti is a messy food for a toddler with a spoon.
senses.exampleCN: 幼儿拿着勺子吃意大利面，吃得满桌都是。
senses.why: If the state of the room is messy, the food or activity that fills it with dirt inherits the same word.
senses.whyCN: 既然房间可以脏乱，那些会把屋子弄得脏乱的食物和活动也顺理成章继承了同一个词。

senses.title: Complicated and unpleasant to deal with
senses.definition: difficult or unpleasant to deal with because it involves confusion, arguments or embarrassing details
senses.definitionCN: 因牵扯混乱、争执或难堪的细节而难以处理、令人不快的
senses.example: Their divorce was long and messy, with lawyers fighting over every asset.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的离婚拖了很久而且很难看，律师为每一项财产都争得不可开交。
senses.why: When affairs are physically out of order, they can also be out of order morally and socially, so a tangled room grows into a tangled lawsuit.
senses.whyCN: 当东西在实处乱作一团，事情在人情事理上也能乱作一团，凌乱的房间于是长成一团乱麻的官司。

senses.title: Not precise or well organized
senses.definition: lacking clear structure or exactness, said of thinking, data, processes or boundaries
senses.definitionCN: 缺少清晰结构或精确性，用于思路、数据、流程或边界
senses.example: The handwriting on the whiteboard was messy, with arrows pointing everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 白板上的字迹潦草混乱，箭头指得到处都是。
senses.why: A page that is physically messy is hard to read; by the same path, a thought or a process that looks like such a page is also messy.
senses.whyCN: 纸面脏乱就难以阅读；循着同一条路，看上去像那种纸面的思路或流程同样被称作 messy。

intro.en: Messy is a straightforward English formation: the noun mess plus the adjectival ending -y, born in the nineteenth century when mess had already shifted from food to disorder.
intro.cn: messy 是一个简单的英语构词：名词 mess 加上形容词词尾 -y，产生于十九世纪，当时 mess 已从「食物」转向「混乱」。

items.en: The story starts far back with the Latin verb mittere, to send, whose participle supplied a name for food sent to the table.
items.cn: 故事要从拉丁语动词 mittere（送）说起，它的分词为「端上桌的食物」提供了名称。

items.en: Old French mes meant a portion or a dish of food, and also the company eating it.
items.cn: 古法语 mes 指一份或一道食物，也指一起进餐的一群人。

items.en: Middle English mess kept the food sense and, from the sixteenth century, began to mean disorder and dirty leftovers.
items.cn: 中古英语 mess 保留了食物义，并在十六世纪起开始表示「混乱」和脏乱的残渣。

items.en: By the nineteenth century mess firmly meant disorder, so English could add the ending -y and form the adjective messy.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，mess 已经稳固地表示「混乱」，英语于是加上词尾 -y 构成形容词 messy。

items.en: From untidy rooms the adjective spread to dirty foods, difficult divorces and imprecise data, covering both real dirt and tangled affairs.
items.cn: 从凌乱的房间出发，这个形容词扩展到弄脏一切的食物、难看的离婚与不精确的数据，既指实物的脏，也指事务的乱。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same Latin sending root; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for dirt and disorder.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「送」词根上的词；近义组收表示脏乱与无序的形容词。

entries.definition: The base noun: an untidy state, dirty waste, or a difficult situation.
entries.definitionCN: messy 的基础名词：凌乱的状态、脏的废弃物或困境。

entries.definition: A piece of information sent to someone, from the same verb of sending.
entries.definitionCN: 送给某人的一条信息，同出拉丁「送」这一动词。

entries.definition: A person who carries a message from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 把消息从一处送到另一处的人。

entries.definition: Not neat, with things left in disorder, but without the strong note of dirt.
entries.definitionCN: 不整洁、东西乱放，但不带 messy 那种「脏」的意味。

entries.definition: Lacking order or arrangement, often said of systems or processes rather than rooms.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏秩序或条理，多用于系统、流程而非房间。

entries.definition: Completely without control or order, a stronger and larger-scale word than messy.
entries.definitionCN: 完全失控、毫无秩序，程度和范围都比 messy 更强。

normalIntro.en: The adjective is built transparently on mess; the family keeps returning to the shared dish of food and the disorder it leaves behind.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词在 mess 上透明地构词而成，同族词反复回到同桌分食的那盘菜，以及饭后留下的凌乱。

normal.en: Messy is simply mess plus -y, meaning full of mess, therefore untidy or dirty.
normal.cn: messy 就是 mess 加 -y，意为「充满 mess」，所以是凌乱的、脏的。

normal.en: The base mess goes back to Latin mittere, to send, through a dish sent to the table.
normal.cn: 基础词 mess 可追溯到拉丁语 mittere（送），经由「被端上桌的一道菜」而来。

normal.en: When mess shifted from food to disorder in the sixteenth century, the ground was ready for the adjective.
normal.cn: 十六世纪 mess 从食物义转向混乱义后，形容词的出现已是水到渠成。

normal.en: Comparative messier and superlative messiest work like any -y adjective: happier, messier.
normal.cn: 比较级 messier、最高级 messiest 的变化方式与所有 -y 形容词一样，如 happier、messier。

normal.en: Messily and messiness are the adverb and the noun of state cut from the same adjective.
normal.cn: messily 和 messiness 是从这个形容词切出的副词与状态名词。

abstract.en: Picture a room after a party of children: every surface holds something that was dropped, not put down.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子们聚会散场后的房间：每个平面放着的都是被丢下的东西，而不是被摆好的东西。

abstract.en: A messy divorce borrows the picture of the dirty room, because a fight over assets leaves emotional stains nobody can wipe off.
abstract.cn: 难看的离婚借用了脏乱房间的画面，因为财产之争留下的情感污渍，谁都擦不掉。

abstract.en: Messy data is a whiteboard nobody finished: arrows everywhere, half the boxes unlabeled.
abstract.cn: 乱糟糟的数据像一块没人写完的白板：箭头乱指，一半方框没有标注。

examples.en: The children's room is terribly messy after they played all afternoon.
examples.cn: 孩子们玩了一下午之后，他们的房间乱得不像话。

examples.en: Their divorce was long and messy, with lawyers fighting over every asset.
examples.cn: 他们的离婚拖了很久而且很难看，律师为每一项财产都争得不可开交。

examples.en: Spaghetti is a messy food for a toddler with a spoon.
examples.cn: 幼儿拿着勺子吃意大利面，吃得满桌都是。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没洗椅」——椅子没洗，房间当然 messy 凌乱。

root: 英语本土构词：名词 mess（混乱；脏乱，源自拉丁语 mittere「送」的分词 missus，经古法语 mes「一份食物」）加形容词词尾 -y，十九世纪成型。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a room full of mess; the adjective spreads from untidy spaces to dirty foods, tangled affairs and imprecise data.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是堆满 mess 的房间；形容词从凌乱的空间扩散到弄脏一切的食物、难缠的事务与不精确的数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a children's room after playtime, blocks across the floor, papers on the bed, spilt juice by the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：玩耍散场后的儿童房，积木铺满地板，画纸摊在床上，门边洒着果汁。

branches.en: blocks and papers left wherever they fell
branches.cn: 积木和画纸掉在哪里就留在哪里

branches.en: a toddler wiping sauce across the table
branches.cn: 幼儿把酱汁抹得满桌都是

branches.en: two lawyers across a table stacked with files
branches.cn: 隔着堆满卷宗的桌子对坐的两位律师

branches.en: a whiteboard full of crossing arrows
branches.cn: 画满交叉箭头的白板

branches.en: gloves and goggles on a lab bench before pouring
branches.cn: 倾倒液体前放在实验台上的手套和护目镜

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin verb of sending, the noun for a dish served, the French form, the English base mess, and the adjectival ending -y.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁「送」动词、指上桌菜食的名词、法语形式、英语基础词 mess，以及形容词词尾 -y 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 宣布；声明；申报
definition_en: to say something officially or firmly
core_image: 一个人举起手，向所有人说明一件事
scene: 主席敲了敲桌子，当众说明会议开始。 The chair declared the meeting open.
sceneCN: 这里 declare 指「宣布」（第 1 个义项：正式公开地说）；句意是主席宣布会议开始。

derivatives.zh: 宣言；声明
陈述的
声明者
未申报的

senses.title: Announce officially
senses.definition: to state something openly in an official way
senses.definitionCN: 以官方的方式公开说明某事
senses.example: The chair declared the meeting open.
senses.exampleCN: 主席宣布会议开始。
senses.why: An official voice turns a private fact into a public one.
senses.whyCN: 官方的声音把私事变成了众人皆知的事。

senses.title: Say firmly
senses.definition: to state a belief with confidence
senses.definitionCN: 很有把握地说出自己的看法
senses.example: She declared that the plan would work.
senses.exampleCN: 她断言这个计划行得通。
senses.why: The word lends a plain sentence the weight of a promise.
senses.whyCN: 这个词给一句普通的话添上了承诺的分量。

senses.title: Report goods to customs
senses.definition: to list goods or money to officials
senses.definitionCN: 向官员列出所带的物品或钱款
senses.example: You must declare any cash over the limit.
senses.exampleCN: 超过限额的现金必须申报。
senses.why: What is hidden must be named before it may pass.
senses.whyCN: 藏着的东西，得先被说出来才能通过。

intro.en: Declare came from Latin declarare, to make clear, from clarus, bright.
intro.cn: declare 来自拉丁语 declarare（使清楚），源于 clarus（明亮的）。

items.en: Clarus meant bright, plain and easy to see.
items.cn: clarus 指明亮的、平白易见的。

items.en: Declarare meant to make a matter bright for all to see.
items.cn: declarare 指把事情照亮，让所有人看见。

items.en: Declarer meant to announce or explain openly.
items.cn: declarer 指公开宣布或解释。

items.en: Declare entered English with the sense of making clear.
items.cn: declare 进入英语时，意思是「说清楚」。

items.en: The customs sense grew from the same idea of naming openly.
items.cn: 海关用法也从「公开说出」这个意思长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the opening and closing sounds, and the meaning group runs from telling to proclaiming.
note.cn: 形近组首尾音相近，近义组则从告知走到宣告。

entries.definition: to speak in a loud, formal way
entries.definitionCN: 以响亮正式的方式讲话

entries.definition: to become smaller or to refuse
entries.definitionCN: 变小，或婉言拒绝

entries.definition: to get something back
entries.definitionCN: 把东西要回来

entries.definition: to tell people about something officially
entries.definitionCN: 正式告诉人们某事

entries.definition: to say something clearly and formally
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而正式地说出

entries.definition: to announce publicly and with force
entries.definitionCN: 公开而有力地宣告

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a gavel on a table and end with a bag opened at a customs desk.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从敲在桌上的小锤开始，落到海关柜台上打开的一只包。

normal.en: To declare is to switch the light on a fact.
normal.cn: declare 就是给一件事实开灯。

normal.en: The chair says three words and the meeting exists.
normal.cn: 主席说三个词，会议才真正开始。

normal.en: What you declare, you can no longer deny.
normal.cn: 你宣布过的事，就再也否认不了。

normal.en: A customs bag is honest only when it is opened.
normal.cn: 海关的包，只有打开时才诚实。

normal.en: Clarus meant bright, and declare still means to bring into the light.
normal.cn: clarus 本指明亮，declare 至今仍是把东西拿到光下。

abstract.en: Picture a gavel coming down once.
abstract.cn: 想象小锤落下一次。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised before a crowd begins to listen.
abstract.cn: 想象人群开始听之前，一只手举了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a bag unzipped under a bright lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一只包在亮灯下被拉开。

examples.en: The chair declared the meeting open.
examples.cn: 主席宣布会议开始。

examples.en: They declared independence in the summer of that year.
examples.cn: 那年夏天他们宣布独立。

examples.en: I have nothing to declare.
examples.cn: 我没有需要申报的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 declare 记成「得客来而」：de 是得，clare 听着像「客来而」，客人一到，主人得当众说一声欢迎。

root: 来自拉丁语 declarare（使清楚），根子是 clarus（明亮的）。十四世纪进入英语时意为「说明、讲清」，后来用于官方场合表示公开宣布，又延伸到向海关如实说明所带物品。

sensesIntro.en: From an official word that starts a meeting, to a firm belief, to goods named at a border.
sensesIntro.cn: 从让会议开始的那句官方话，到坚定的看法，再到在关口说清的物品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand making one fact public.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手举起，把一件事变成公开的。

branches.en: The first sense is the official voice that changes a situation.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是改变局面的那声官方宣布。

branches.en: The second sense is a person speaking with full confidence.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一个人满有把握地说话。

branches.en: The third sense is the same act performed for the state.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是同一个动作，只是对国家做。

branches.en: A meeting and a border both wait for someone to speak first.
branches.cn: 会议和关口，都在等一个人先开口。

branches.en: Firmness and honesty are the same tone in different rooms.
branches.cn: 坚定和如实，是不同场合里的同一种语气。

intro.en: Declare and its noun declaration carry the whole clar- family of clearness.
intro.cn: declare 及其名词 declaration 带着整个 clar- 家族，都与「清楚」有关。

latinIntro.en: The root is clarus, bright; clarare meant to make bright.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 clarus（明亮），clarare 意为使明亮。

items.example: They declared the winner at once.
items.exampleCN: 他们立刻宣布了获胜者。

items.example: The declaration was signed by all.
A declarative sentence ends with a full stop.

items.exampleCN: 那项裁定只是宣告性质的。

Their declared goal is zero waste.
items.exampleCN: 他们公开的目标是零浪费。
未申报的收入必须纳税。

items.meaning: to announce a state of war

items.exampleCN: 这个国家在黎明时宣战。

definition_zh: 智力；智慧；情报
definition_en: the ability to learn, understand, and reason, or secret information about an enemy
core_image: 有人在棋盘上看清十几步后的局面，同时有人把密信交到暗处
scene: 实验室里摆着拼图、棋子和一套做记录的量表，受试者正埋头解题。 Tests of intelligence rarely capture how quickly a child learns.
sceneCN: 这里 intelligence 是「智力」（第 1 个义项：学习、理解与推理的能力），句意为智力测验很少能捕捉孩子学得多快。画面里的物件：拼图、棋子、记录表。

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「聪明的」
由 intelligent 加 -ly 构成，义为「明智地」
由词干加 -ible 构成，义为「可理解的」
由同一词干构成，义为「智力的」

senses.title: The power to learn and reason
senses.definition: the general ability to learn facts, understand ideas, and solve problems
senses.definitionCN: 学习事实、理解观念并解决问题的总体能力
senses.example: Her intelligence showed less in tests than in the questions she asked.
senses.exampleCN: 她的智力更多体现在提的问题里，而不是分数里。
senses.why: Latin intellegere, "to understand", gives the noun its core of understanding.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intellegere「理解」给这个名词以「理解」的内核。

senses.title: Secret information
senses.definition: information gathered about an enemy or rival, often secretly
senses.definitionCN: 常以秘密方式收集的关于敌方或对手的信息
senses.example: Naval intelligence warned the fleet two days ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 海军情报提前两天警告了舰队。
senses.why: This sense grew in military writing in the sixteenth century, where knowledge itself is a weapon.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项在十六世纪的军事写作中成长起来，在那里知识本身就是武器。

senses.title: A mind or being that knows
senses.definition: a thinking being, or in modern use a machine that seems to think
senses.definitionCN: 会思考的生灵，或现代用法中指看似会思考的机器
senses.example: Scientists argue about whether any machine intelligence can be friendly.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家在争论机器智能是否可能是友善的。
senses.why: The word shifts from a power to the possessor of that power.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一种能力转向拥有这种能力的主体。

senses.title: News or information
senses.definition: formal or old-fashioned news about some event
senses.definitionCN: 关于某事的正式或旧式说法「消息」
senses.example: The family waited for intelligence from the frontier.
senses.exampleCN: 家人等着边疆传来的消息。
senses.why: The oldest English use simply meant tidings brought by a messenger.
senses.whyCN: 最早的英语用法只指信使带来的音信。

intro.en: Intelligence is the Latin noun intelligentia, built on intellegere "to understand".
intro.cn: intelligence 是拉丁语名词 intelligentia，建构在 intellegere「理解」之上。

items.en: Legere "to gather, read" with inter- "among" yields intellegere, "to pick out the sense".
items.cn: legere「采集、读」与 inter-「在……之间」合成 intellegere「辨出意义」。

items.en: Intelligentia named the power of understanding in classical philosophy.
items.cn: intelligentia 在古典哲学中指理解的能力。

items.en: French intelligence carried both understanding and news.
items.cn: 法语 intelligence 既指理解，也指消息。

items.en: English kept both senses; the news sense later narrowed to military and secret reports.
items.cn: 英语保留了两种意义；消息义后来窄化为军事与秘密报告。

items.en: The twentieth century added artificial intelligence and machine intelligence.
items.cn: 二十世纪添上了人工智能与机器智能的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the understanding root; the near-meaning group holds words about mental power.
note.cn: 形近组共享「理解」词根；近义组收表示心智能力的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for a person or animal that learns well.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容人或动物学习能力强。

entries.definition: The faculty of reasoning, in the abstract.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，抽象地指推理能力。

entries.definition: Able to be understood by the hearer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能被听懂看懂的」。

entries.definition: The same power seen as a separate faculty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，把同一能力看作单独的官能。

entries.definition: Good judgement gained from experience, not speed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「智慧」，来自经验而非反应快。

entries.definition: Facts of any kind, open or secret.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信息」，公开或秘密的事实。

normalIntro.en: The hooks join the legere root of reading to the two faces of the word: mind and secret news.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把「读」这一词根 legere 与这个词的两张面孔合起来：心智与秘密消息。

normal.en: intellegere: to read among things means to understand them.
normal.cn: intellegere：在事物之间读懂，就是理解它们。

normal.en: Artificial intelligence is still only a clever reader of patterns.
normal.cn: 人工智能仍只是个会读图案的聪明角色。

normal.en: Military intelligence is information treated as a weapon.
normal.cn: 军事情报是被当作武器的信息。

normal.en: Intelligence tests measure only what tests can measure.
normal.cn: 智力测验只能测出测验能测的东西。

normal.en: The same root gives intelligent and intelligible.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 intelligent 与 intelligible。

abstract.en: Intelligence is the mind finding a path where none was drawn.
abstract.cn: 智力是头脑在没有路的地方找出路。

abstract.en: Knowing the enemy is half the battle, hence intelligence.
abstract.cn: 知敌者半胜，所以有情报之说。

abstract.en: A quiet question can show more intelligence than a quick answer.
abstract.cn: 一个安静的问题可能比一个快速回答更能显出智力。

examples.en: The puzzle is designed to test spatial intelligence.
examples.cn: 这个拼图用来测试空间智力。

examples.en: Intelligence from the coast reached the capital by noon.
examples.cn: 来自海岸的情报到正午已抵达首都。

examples.en: The firm hired her for her unusual social intelligence.
examples.cn: 这家公司聘她，是因为她不同寻常的社交智慧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特立先生」——那位先生脑子好，还掌握情报

root: 拉丁语 legere「采集、读」→ inter- + legere → intellegere「理解」→ intelligentia「理解力」→ 古法语 intelligence（理解；消息）→ 英语 intelligence。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: mental power, secret information, a thinking being, and old-fashioned news.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：心智能力、秘密情报、有智力的生灵，以及旧式的「消息」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one mind reads the whole board while a sealed note changes hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗头脑读透整盘棋，同时一封密封的纸条在暗中转手。

branches.en: THE TEST ROOM: puzzles measure how quickly a mind learns.
branches.cn: 测试室这条线：拼图衡量头脑学得多快。

branches.en: THE SEALED NOTE: knowledge about a rival is guarded.
branches.cn: 密信这条线：关于对手的知识被小心保守。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: a thinking being also takes the name.
branches.cn: 机器这条线：会思考的主体也用这个词。

branches.en: THE MESSENGER: plain news from far away.
branches.cn: 信使这条线：远方传来的普通消息。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses are knowledge put to use.
branches.cn: 连接线：两个义项都是被派上用场的知识。

intro.en: Intelligence = inter- "between" + leg- "read" + -ence, a noun of state.
intro.cn: intelligence = inter-「在……之间」+ leg-「读」+ -ence，表示状态的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin intelligentia is recorded; the deeper layer alone is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intelligentia 有记载，只有更深一层属于重构。

items.example: It also appears in legend and lecture.
items.exampleCN: 也见于 legend 与 lecture。

definition_zh: 治疗；疗法；对待；处理；处理方式
definition_en: the care given to cure an illness or injury, or the way a person or thing is dealt with
core_image: 病床边挂着输液袋，护士按表一格一格记录换药
scene: 住院部的床头挂着卡片，护士按上面的疗程逐日换药记录。 The new treatment reduced the pain within a week.
sceneCN: 这里 treatment 是「治疗、疗法」（第 1 个义项：为治愈而给的医疗照护）；句意为新疗法一周内就减轻了疼痛。床头那张逐日记录的卡片正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -ment 还原为动词，义为「对待；治疗」
由 treat 加 -able 构成，义为「可治疗的」
加前缀 mis- 构成，义为「虐待」

senses.title: Medical care for an illness
senses.definition: the care and medicine given to cure a disease or injury
senses.definitionCN: 为治愈疾病或伤处而给的照护与药物
senses.example: She is receiving treatment for the infection.
senses.exampleCN: 她正在接受感染治疗。
senses.why: Treating a patient is handling the body back to health, and the noun names that handling.
senses.whyCN: 治疗病人就是把身体料理回健康，名词指的就是这份料理。

senses.title: A particular method of healing
senses.definition: a specific way of treating a disease
senses.definitionCN: 治疗某种病的具体办法
senses.example: The clinic offers two treatments for the knee.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所对膝关节有两种疗法。
senses.why: Once methods are compared, the noun shifts from care in general to one named method.
senses.whyCN: 一旦比较各种方法，名词就从笼统的照护转向某一种有名字的疗法。

senses.title: The way a person is dealt with
senses.definition: the way someone is behaved towards
senses.definitionCN: 别人对待某人的方式
senses.example: The workers asked for fair treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们要求公平对待。
senses.why: The oldest sense of treat is to behave towards, so treatment is simply how that behaves out.
senses.whyCN: treat 最老的含义就是「朝向某人的行为」，treatment 就是把这种行为表现出的样子。

senses.title: A process applied to a material
senses.definition: a process that is applied to a substance to change it
senses.definitionCN: 为使物质改变而施加的工序
senses.example: The water needs chemical treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 这水需要化学处理。
senses.why: Handling a material is the same handling as handling a person, only without feeling.
senses.whyCN: 处理材料与待人同属「处理」，只是对象没有感情。

senses.title: A way of presenting a subject
senses.definition: the way a writer or artist deals with a subject
senses.definitionCN: 作者或艺术家处理题材的方式
senses.example: Her treatment of the war is very restrained.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这场战争的处理很克制。
senses.why: Tractare also meant to discuss, so how a subject is discussed is its treatment.
senses.whyCN: tractare 也有讨论义，所以一个题目被怎样讨论，就是它的「处理方式」。

intro.en: The noun is treat plus -ment, and treat comes from Latin tractare, to handle.
intro.cn: 这个名词是 treat 加 -ment，而 treat 出自拉丁语 tractare（处理）。

items.en: Tractare is the frequentative of trahere, to draw, and means to keep handling.
items.cn: tractare 是 trahere（拉）的反复形式，意为反复摆弄。

items.en: Traitier gives the English verb treat, for dealing with people and matters.
items.cn: 古法语 traitier 生出英语动词 treat，用于待人与处事。

items.en: The -ment ending turns the verb into a noun of the handling itself.
items.cn: -ment 词尾把动词变成表示「处理本身」的名词。

items.en: Medicine makes the medical sense the dominant one in modern use.
items.cn: 现代用法中，医学义成了最主要的义项。

items.en: Industry and journalism extend it to water, waste, and the handling of subjects.
items.cn: 工业与新闻业把它扩展到水、废物与题材的处理上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the treat- stem, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for care and handling.
note.cn: 形近组共用 treat- 词干，近义组汇集表示照护与处理的其他说法。

entries.definition: to behave towards, or give care
entries.definitionCN: 对待；治疗

entries.definition: a formal written agreement
entries.definitionCN: 条约

entries.definition: a long written work
entries.definitionCN: 论著

entries.definition: cruel or unfair handling
entries.definitionCN: 虐待；不公对待

entries.definition: treatment to cure a condition
entries.definitionCN: 疗法；治疗

entries.definition: medicine used to treat illness
entries.definitionCN: 药物；用药

entries.definition: a treatment that makes someone well
entries.definitionCN: 疗法；治愈
