entries.definitionCN: 处理；操作

normalIntro.en: Treat plus -ment: the verb known, the noun follows.
normalIntro.cn: 在 treat 后加上 -ment，动词认识了，名词就跟着来。

normal.en: Treat is to handle, and -ment makes that handling into a thing.
normal.cn: treat 是处理，-ment 把这份处理变成一样东西。

normal.en: Treatment in a hospital is handling a body back to health.
normal.cn: 医院里的 treatment 是把身体料理回健康。

normal.en: Mistreatment adds mis-, meaning handling the wrong way.
normal.cn: mistreatment 加 mis-，意为用错方式对待。

normal.en: Water treatment plants handle water, not patients.
normal.cn: 水处理厂处理的是水，不是病人。

normal.en: The word appears in headlines about fair and unfair handling alike.
normal.cn: 这个词既见于公平对待的标题，也见于不公对待的标题。

abstract.en: Picture a card at the head of a hospital bed, ticked each day.
abstract.cn: 想象床头一张卡片，每天打一个勾。

abstract.en: Hear the drip counted in drops.
abstract.cn: 听输液一滴一滴地数。

abstract.en: Then move the same careful tick to a water tank and to a worker’s pay.
abstract.cn: 再把同样的仔细勾画挪到水池与工人的工资上。

examples.en: He began treatment for the disease last spring.
examples.cn: 他去年春天开始接受该病的治疗。

examples.en: The staff received training in the fair treatment of patients.
examples.cn: 员工接受了公平对待病人的培训。

examples.en: The plant provides treatment for waste water.
examples.cn: 这座工厂负责废水的处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹特门」——吹一口气特别把门关好，小心护理，这就是治疗。

root: 拉丁语 tractare（处理）+ 后缀 -ment，由动词 treat 构成；同族有 treat、treaty、treatise、mistreatment

sensesIntro.en: The word covers handling of every kind, with healing as the most familiar branch.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖各种各样的「处理」，其中以治疗最为人熟悉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a card at a hospital bed, ticked once each day.
core.cn: 核心意象：床头一张卡片，每天打一个勾。

branches.en: The healing sense, first as care, then as a named method.
branches.cn: 治疗义：先是照护，再是具体的疗法。

branches.en: The fairness sense, how people behave towards people.
branches.cn: 公平义：人与人之间怎样相待。

branches.en: The industrial sense, where a material is the patient.
branches.cn: 工业义：被处理的是材料。

branches.en: The artistic sense, how a subject is presented.
branches.cn: 艺术义：一个题材被怎样呈现。

branches.en: The method sense, where a named cure is chosen.
branches.cn: 方法义：选出一种有名字的治法。

intro.en: The noun adds a Latin suffix to a French verb of handling.
intro.cn: 这个名词给一个法语「处理」动词加上拉丁名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The tract- stem runs through treat, treatment, treaty, contract, and extract.
latinIntro.cn: tract- 词干贯穿 treat、treatment、treaty、contract 与 extract。

definition_zh: 民族；国家；全体国民；（历史用法）部落、族群
definition_en: a people who share a common origin, history or identity, especially when organized as a state
core_image: 一条手绘的边界线穿过同一片口音相同的村庄，把同一个集市分成两半
scene: 旧地图铺在桌上，一条边界线正好穿过说同一种口音的几个村庄，教书的人用手指顺着线划过。 The nation was divided by a border drawn through its villages.
sceneCN: 这里 nation 指「共享同一种身份与语言的一群人」（第 2 个义项：以共同出身、语言或历史凝聚的群体，未必与国家疆界重合）；句意为这个民族被一条穿过其村庄的边界分成了两半。图中可辨识物件：旧地图、铅笔画的边界、被切开的集市、手指；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 民族；国家；全体国民（可数，复数 nations）

collocations.zh: 一个由移民构成的国家

derivatives.zh: 国家的；民族的（nation 加 -al，指属于整个民族的）
国籍；民族（national 加 -ity，指法律或族群身份）
民族主义（national 加 -ism，指以民族为中心的主张）
民族主义者；民族主义的（national 加 -ist）
收归国有；使全国化（national 加 -ize，使转为国家所有）
出生；诞生（拉丁 nasci 加 -ity，与 nation 同出「出生」词根）
本地的；本地人（拉丁 nativus，同出 nasci「出生」）

senses.title: A sovereign country
senses.definition: an independent state with its own government, territory and seat at international bodies
senses.definitionCN: 拥有自己的政府、领土与国际组织席位的独立国家
senses.example: The two nations opened embassies within a year of the ceasefire.
senses.exampleCN: 停火一年之内，这两个国家互设了大使馆。
senses.why: Because a people organized as a state is the modern default, the plain everyday sense of the word is simply 'country'.
senses.whyCN: 因为「组织成国家的一群人」是现代默认形态，所以这个词最日常的意思就是「国家」。

senses.title: A people sharing identity
senses.definition: a group held together by a common language, history or sense of belonging, whether or not it has a state
senses.definitionCN: 由共同语言、历史或归属感凝聚的群体，无论是否拥有国家
senses.example: The nation was divided by a border drawn through its villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这个民族被一条穿过其村庄的边界分成了两半。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a people born together, and that sense survives precisely where the state and the people do not match.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「同出一源的一群人」，这一意思恰恰在国家与人群不重合之处延续下来。

senses.title: The citizenry taken as one body
senses.definition: the whole body of citizens, often addressed as a single moral actor in speeches
senses.definitionCN: 全体公民的整体，常在演说中被当作单一的道义行动者来称呼
senses.example: The nation was asked to give up one holiday to fund the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 全体国民被要求放弃一个假日，为医院筹资。
senses.why: Once everyone is imagined as one body, speakers can address the whole population as a single person who decides.
senses.whyCN: 一旦所有人被想象成一个整体，演说者就能把全体人口当作一个做决定的单数人格来称呼。

senses.title: A tribe or ethnic people in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法中的部落或族群
senses.definition: a people or tribe described in history and anthropology, as in the nations of the ancient Near East
senses.definitionCN: 历史学与人类学中描述的族群或部落，如古代近东诸族
senses.example: The chronicle lists the nations that sent tribute to the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这部编年史列出了向都城进贡的各族。
senses.why: Natio in Latin could mean any group of common birth, and that broad sense passed into older English historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 natio 可指任何同出一源的群体，这一宽泛含义进入了较早的英语历史写作。

senses.title: A formally recognized tribal nation
senses.titleCN: 获正式承认的原住民族
senses.definition: the official self-designation of many Native American peoples, as in the Navajo Nation
senses.definitionCN: 许多北美原住民族群的正式自称，如纳瓦霍族
senses.example: The tribal council speaks for the nation in negotiations with the federal government.
senses.exampleCN: 部落议会在与联邦政府的谈判中代表该民族发言。
senses.why: Sovereignty language was borrowed from international law, so tribes adopted 'nation' to assert a political status older than the state.
senses.whyCN: 主权话语借自国际法，因此各部落采用「nation」来主张一种比国家更古老的政治地位。

senses.title: The community of states
senses.titleCN: 国际社会中的国家共同体
senses.definition: the collectivity of states acting together, as in 'the community of nations' or 'the family of nations'
senses.definitionCN: 共同行动的各国整体，如「国际社会」「国家大家庭」
senses.example: The community of nations voted to send observers.
senses.exampleCN: 国际社会投票决定派出观察员。
senses.why: When states are treated as persons in international law, their society is naturally described as a group of nations.
senses.whyCN: 当国家在国际法中被当作人格，它们的共同体自然就被描述为一群国家。

senses.title: A student nation at older universities
senses.titleCN: 旧式大学中的学生同乡会
senses.definition: a regional association of students at historic Scandinavian and other European universities
senses.definitionCN: 北欧及欧洲其他历史悠久的大学中，按地区组成的学生团体
senses.example: He joined the northern nation and ate at its hall every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他加入了北方学生同乡会，每晚都在其食堂吃饭。
senses.why: The word once meant simply a group of people of common origin, which is exactly what a regional student society is.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾经只表示同出一源的一群人，而按地区组成的学生团体正是如此。

senses.title: A rhetorical collective of like-minded people
senses.titleCN: 修辞上指志趣相同的一群人
senses.definition: a figurative use such as 'a nation of readers' or 'a nation of shopkeepers', naming a large group by its shared habit
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，如「阅读的民族」「店主的国家」，以共同习惯命名一大群人
senses.example: The magazine called its subscribers a nation of careful readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志把它的订户称为一个认真阅读的民族。
senses.why: The rhetorical force comes from treating a shared practice as a common birth, which is the word's original image.
senses.whyCN: 这种修辞力量来自把共同习惯当作共同出身，而这正是这个词最初的意象。

intro.en: Nation comes from a Latin noun of birth, narrowed in French toward a political people and then widened again in English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nation 来自一个表示出生的拉丁名词，在法语中被收窄为政治意义上的国民，进入英语后又重新变宽。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nasci 'to be born' is generally thought to descend from a root meaning 'to beget', the same stock as gignere 'to produce' and genus 'race, kind'.
items.cn: nasci「出生」一般认为源自表示「生育」的词根，与 gignere「产生」、genus「种族、种类」同族。

items.en: Natio first named a birth or an origin, then a body of people of common birth; Roman writers also used it for foreigners living in one quarter of the city.
items.cn: natio 最初指出生或出身，继而指同出一源的一群人；罗马作家也用它指聚居城中一区的异邦人。

items.en: Old French nation narrowed the word to a political people or a province, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 nation 把词义收窄为政治意义上的国民或一个行省，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: English first used the word for a people of common stock, then for the whole political community of a kingdom, then for a sovereign state.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指同出一源的族群，继而指一个王国中的整体政治共同体，再指主权国家。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries the word was joined to -state and -hood, and the pairing of nation and state became the normal form of political organization.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪，这个词与 state、hood 组合，民族与国家的配对成为常见的政治组织形式。

items.en: Source uncertain (dates and reconstruction): the exact point at which the word shifted from a birth-group to a sovereign state is not recorded, and the pre-Latin root form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（年代与重构）：从出生群体转向主权国家的确切时点没有记载；拉丁语之前的词根形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the birth root and are constantly confused; group two holds words for the same large entity seen from different angles.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「出生」词根、极易混淆的词；第二组是从不同角度指同一大实体的词。

entries.definition: The status of belonging to a state in law, or to an ethnic group; it names a status, while nation names the group itself.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上属于某国的身份，或属于某族群的身份；它指身份，而 nation 指群体本身。

entries.definition: The adjective 'of a nation', needed before a noun; it cannot stand for the people themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「国家的、民族的」形容词，须置于名词前，不能直接代替人群本身。

entries.definition: The doctrine built on nation; it is a belief about nations, not a nation.
entries.definitionCN: 建立在 nation 之上的学说，是关于民族的信念，而非民族本身。

entries.definition: The fact of being born, or a birth scene in art; the root is literal birth rather than a political people.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生这一事实，或艺术中的诞生场景；词根取「出生」字面义，而非政治人群。

entries.definition: The political and legal apparatus with borders and sovereignty; a nation may exist without one, a state may hold several.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有边界与主权的政治法律机构；民族可以没有国家，国家也可以包含多个民族。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a land and its people; it stresses territory rather than shared identity.
entries.definitionCN: 指一片土地及其人民的日常用词，侧重领土而非共同身份。

entries.definition: A body of persons considered together; it can mean the same as nation but carries no claim to a state.
entries.definitionCN: 被整体看待的一群人；可与民族同义，但不含建国主张。

entries.definition: A group defined by ancestry, language and culture; it is the social-science term where nation carries political weight.
entries.definitionCN: 以祖先、语言与文化界定的群体；这是社会科学术语，而 nation 带有政治分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nasci 'be born' plus -io gives natio, a people of common birth, and English shortened natio to nation.
normal.cn: nasci「出生」加 -io 得 natio，即同出一源的一群人，英语把 natio 缩为 nation。

normal.en: The same birth root gives native, nativity and nature, so all three share the idea of what one is born with.
normal.cn: 同一「出生」词根还给出 native、nativity、nature，三者都含「与生俱来」的意思。

normal.en: The family runs nation, national, nationality, nationalism, nationalist, nationalize.
normal.cn: 同族词依次是 nation、national、nationality、nationalism、nationalist、nationalize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: sovereign nation, a nation of immigrants, a nation without a state.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：主权国家、移民国家、没有国家的民族。

normal.en: The compound nation-state exists precisely because nation and state can come apart.
normal.cn: nation-state 这一复合词之所以存在，正因为民族与国家可能分离。

abstract.en: Picture a family album whose pages are used as a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一本家族相册，它的书页被当作地图来用。

abstract.en: Picture a border post standing in the middle of one orchard.
abstract.cn: 想象一座边界哨站立在同一个果园的正中间。

abstract.cn: 想象同一个合唱团在两个分开的房间里唱同一首歌。

examples.en: The nation rebuilt its railways with money borrowed from abroad.
examples.cn: 这个国家用向外国借来的钱重建了铁路。

examples.en: A nation can outlive the state that claims to represent it.
examples.cn: 一个民族可以比声称代表它的国家活得更久。

examples.en: The census asks people to state their nation as well as their citizenship.
examples.cn: 人口普查要求人们同时填写民族与国籍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「na（那）+ tion（人群）」——那一片同出一源的人 → 民族、国家

root: 拉丁 natio「出生、出身、族群」，出自 nasci「出生」；与 gignere「产生」、genus「种族」一般认为是同一词族。英语 nation 兼指民族与国家，因为二者常被视为一体。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one birth-group: people of common origin become a country, a citizenry, a tribe, a recognized tribal nation, a society of states, a student society, and finally any large group sharing a habit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「出生群体」展开：同出一源的人依次成为国家、全体国民、部落、获承认的原住民族、国家共同体、学生同乡会，最后成为任何共享习惯的大群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn around people of common birth, which later becomes a border on a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：围绕同出一源的人画一条线，这条线后来变成地图上的国界。

branches.en: STATE AND SOCIETY: one nation is a country, many nations together are the international community.
branches.cn: 国家与国际社会：单个民族是国家，众多国家合起来是国际社会。

branches.en: PEOPLE WITHOUT A STATE: a nation can be split by a border or organized as a student society.
branches.cn: 无国家的人群：民族可以被边界切开，也可以组织成学生同乡会。

branches.en: ONE BODY: the citizenry is addressed as a single moral person.
branches.cn: 一个整体：全体国民被当作单一的道义人格来称呼。

branches.en: TRIBAL NATION: history and law both use the word for peoples organized by descent.
branches.cn: 部落民族：历史学与法学都用这个词指按血缘组织的人群。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE GROUP: any shared habit can be played as a common birth.
branches.cn: 比喻群体：任何共同习惯都可以被当作共同出身来用。

intro.en: Nation is a Latin noun of birth with a state suffix, and the same stem then feeds nationality, nationalism and national.
intro.cn: nation 是一个表示出生、带状态后缀的拉丁名词，同一词干又衍生出 nationality、nationalism、national。

latinIntro.en: Nasci supplies the verb, -io makes a noun of state, and natio is the result; -al and -itas extend the family.
latinIntro.cn: nasci 提供动词，-io 构成状态名词，natio 即其结果；-al 与 -itas 再扩展整个词族。

items.cn: cohors 意为围起的院子或一队士兵。

items.en: The word named both the yard and the guard around a leader.

items.en: Cort named the yard of a castle and the lord's household.
items.cn: cort 指城堡的院子和领主的家眷随从。

items.en: It now names law courts, ball courts and royal households.

senses.exampleCN: 这座城市委托建造了一座新桥。
senses.why: To commission is to entrust the making of something to another person.
senses.whyCN: 委托就是把某物的制作托付给别人。

intro.cn: commission 来自拉丁语 commissio（交托），源自 committere（托付）。

items.en: Committere joined com-, together, with mittere, to send.
items.cn: committere 把表示一起的 com- 与表示送出的 mittere 结合。

items.en: Commissio named the act of entrusting a task.
items.cn: commissio 指把任务托付出去的行为。

items.en: Old French commission carried the sense of an authority given.
items.cn: 古法语 commission 带有授予权限的含义。

items.cn: 英语 commission 最初指正式的授权命令。

items.en: It split into a group, a share of a sale and the act of ordering work.

definition_zh: 指责；控告；归咎；指控
definition_en: to say that someone has done something wrong, or to charge them formally with a crime
core_image: 一根手指直直指向对面的人，屋里所有人的目光都跟着转过去
scene: 会议室里有人把文件摔在桌上，声音一下子冷了下来。 She accused him of hiding the report.
sceneCN: 这里 accuse 指当面指出对方做了错事（第 1 个义项：指责）；句意为她指责他把报告藏了起来。

pos.zh: 动词：指责；控告；归咎；指控

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「指控；指责」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「指控者；原告」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ory 构成，义为「指责的；控诉的」
由现在分词 accusing 加 -ly 构成，义为「带着责备地」

senses.title: To say someone did wrong
senses.definition: to say to someone's face that they have done something wrong, unfair or unacceptable
senses.definitionCN: 当着某人的面说他做了错事、不公道的事或不可接受的事
senses.example: She accused him of hiding the report.
senses.exampleCN: 她指责他把报告藏了起来。
senses.why: Latin causa is a legal case, and accusare began as 'to bring a case against'; everyday blame is that courtroom gesture carried into ordinary rooms.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 causa 指「诉讼案件」，accusare 原本是「对某人提起诉讼」；日常的指责就是把法庭上那个手势搬进了普通房间。

senses.title: To charge with a crime
senses.definition: to state formally in court or in a police statement that someone has committed a crime
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭或警方陈述中正式指出某人犯了罪
senses.example: The company was accused of tax fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司被控税务欺诈。
senses.why: The courtroom is the oldest home of the word: to accuse is to state a charge that a court must answer.
senses.whyCN: 法庭是这个词最古老的家：accuse 就是提出一项需要法庭回应的指控。

senses.title: To blame a thing as the cause
senses.definition: to name a factory, policy, habit or other impersonal thing as the cause of harm
senses.definitionCN: 把损害的原因归到工厂、政策、习惯等非人的事物头上
senses.example: Many accuse social media of making young people anxious.
senses.exampleCN: 许多人把年轻人的焦虑归咎于社交媒体。
senses.why: If a case can be brought against a person, it can also be brought against anything that causes harm.
senses.whyCN: 既然可以对一个人提起诉讼，也就可以对任何造成损害的事物提起诉讼，于是它长出了「归咎于事物」的用法。

senses.title: To blame oneself
senses.definition: to say that you yourself have done something wrong, in the pattern accuse oneself
senses.definitionCN: 用 accuse oneself 的结构表示认定自己做错了事
senses.example: She accused herself of not calling sooner.
senses.exampleCN: 她责怪自己没有早点打电话。
senses.why: The accusing finger can turn back towards the speaker; the same charge is then laid on oneself.
senses.whyCN: 指责的手指也可以转回来指向说话者自己，同一项指控就落在了自己身上。

senses.title: The person charged in court
senses.definition: in the phrase the accused, the person or people charged with a crime in a court case
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the accused 这一说法，指刑事案件中被控犯罪的人
senses.example: The accused sat quietly beside her lawyer.
senses.exampleCN: 被告安静地坐在她的律师身旁。
senses.why: A charge needs someone standing in the dock, and the passive participle became the name for that person.
senses.whyCN: 指控需要一个站在被告席上的人，被动分词就变成了那个人的称呼。

senses.title: A blaming look or tone
senses.definition: of a look, tone or gesture, showing that you think someone has done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 指目光、语气或动作表示出认定对方做错了事
senses.example: He gave me an accusing look across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他隔着桌子责备地看了我一眼。
senses.why: A pointing finger is a visible charge, so the participle also describes a look or tone that points without words.
senses.whyCN: 指着人的手指本身就是看得见的指控，于是分词也用来形容不用说话就在指人的目光或语气。

senses.title: To allege in an official report
senses.definition: to state publicly in a report, an investigation or the media that a person or group has done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 在报告、调查或媒体上公开指出某人或某群体做了错事
senses.example: The report accuses two officials of taking bribes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告指控两名官员收受贿赂。
senses.why: A case can be opened in public as well as in private; a report performs the same act before a wider court.
senses.whyCN: 案件既可以在私下提出，也可以在公众面前提出；一份报告就是在更大的法庭上做同一件事。

senses.title: To be wrongly blamed
senses.definition: of an innocent person, to be blamed for something they did not do, often in the phrase wrongly accused
senses.definitionCN: 指无辜的人被扣上并非自己所为的事，常见于 wrongly accused 这一说法
senses.example: He was wrongly accused and spent two years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 他被冤枉入狱两年。
senses.why: Because a charge can be false, the passive form carries the shadow of injustice: being accused is not the same as being guilty.
senses.whyCN: 指控可能是假的，所以被动形式也带着不公的阴影：被指控并不等于有罪。

intro.en: Accuse comes from Latin accusare 'to bring a charge', built on causa, the word for a legal case; the courtroom sense came first and the everyday one followed.
intro.cn: accuse 来自拉丁语 accusare「提出指控」，建立在表示「诉讼案件」的 causa 之上；法庭义在先，日常责怪义随后。

items.en: Causa meant 'cause, reason, motive' and also 'a legal case'; the legal sense is the one that shaped accuse.
items.cn: causa 意为「原因、理由、动机」，也指「诉讼案件」；塑造 accuse 的正是法律那一层意思。

items.en: Causari 'to plead, dispute, give as a reason' is a verb formed on causa.
items.cn: causari 意为「申辩、争讼、提出理由」，是由 causa 构成的动词。

items.en: Ad- 'to, against' plus causari gave accusare, 'to call to account, bring a charge against'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向、对着」加 causari 构成 accusare，意为「要求对账、提出指控」。

items.en: Old French acuser, recorded in the twelfth century, carried both the legal charge and the everyday blame.
items.cn: 古法语 acuser 见于十二世纪，同时带着法律指控与日常责怪两层意思。

items.en: English borrowed the verb around 1300; the legal and the personal senses have travelled together ever since.
items.cn: 英语约在 1300 年借入这个动词；法律义与针对个人的责怪义从此一直同行。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word's own family plus one Latin relative with a different prefix; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of blaming and formal charging.
note.cn: 形近组是这个词自己的词族，加上一个换了前缀的拉丁亲属词；近义组收表示责怪与正式指控的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「正式控告」，多用于警方与法庭的正式程序。

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「正式起诉」，多指美国司法中对重罪的正式起诉。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root causa and the fixed patterns accuse actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 causa，以及 accuse 实际使用的固定结构。

normal.en: Causa is a case: to accuse is to bring a case against someone.
normal.cn: causa 是「案件」：accuse 就是对人提起一桩案子。

normal.en: The prefix ad- points forward, and so does the finger.
normal.cn: 前缀 ad- 朝前指，那根指责的手指也朝前指。

normal.en: The pattern is accuse someone of something, never accuse someone for something.
normal.cn: 固定结构是 accuse somebody of something，而不是用 for。

normal.en: The accused is the person standing in the dock, not the person speaking.
normal.cn: the accused 指站在被告席上的那个人，不是说话的人。

normal.en: An accusing look does the same work as a spoken charge, only without words.
normal.cn: 责备的目光做的是同一件事，只是没有说出口。

abstract.en: Picture one finger held out across a table while every other head turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指隔着桌子伸出去，其余的头都转了过来。

abstract.en: A charge is a line drawn around a person; the word is about where that line is placed.
abstract.cn: 指控就是在一个人周围画一条线；这个词关心的就是这条线画在哪里。

abstract.en: Because the line can be drawn wrongly, the word always carries the risk of injustice.
abstract.cn: 因为这条线可能画错，这个词永远带着不公的风险。

branches.en: THE POINTED CHARGE: blame aimed at a person face to face, or at a thing that causes harm.
branches.cn: 当面指责线：把责任当面指向一个人，或指向造成损害的事物。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CHARGE: the court and the public report both state an allegation that must be answered.
branches.cn: 正式指控线：法庭与公开报告都在提出一项需要回应的指控。

branches.en: THE TURNED FINGER: the same charge can be laid on the speaker.
branches.cn: 回指线：同一项指控也可以落在说话者自己身上。

branches.en: THE DOCK: the passive participle names the person the charge is aimed at.
branches.cn: 被告席线：被动分词用来称呼被指控的那个人。

branches.en: THE UNSpoken CHARGE: a look can accuse without words, and a false charge leaves the mark of injustice.

examples.en: The engine runs at three thousand revolutions per minute.
examples.cn: 这台发动机每分钟转三千圈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ volution（转）」——转一整圈，就是旋转、革命。

root: 拉丁语 revolvere（滚回）→ revolutio（翻转）→ 法语 revolution → revolution，核心义「整圈翻转」。

sensesIntro.en: Revolution starts with political overthrow, extends to any complete change, and keeps the physical sense of one full turn.
sensesIntro.cn: revolution 从政治推翻开始，延伸到任何彻底变革，同时保留转一整圈的物理含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fallen statue, a new flag and a turning wheel.
core.cn: 核心意象：倒下的雕像、新的旗帜与转动的巨轮。

branches.en: Political overthrow is the public sense.
branches.cn: 政治推翻是公共层面的含义。

branches.en: Any deep change can be called a revolution.
branches.cn: 任何深刻变化都能称为革命。

branches.en: One full turn keeps the oldest meaning.
branches.cn: 整圈转动保留了最古老的含义。

branches.en: Politics and technology both turn the old order over.
branches.cn: 政治与技术都翻转了旧秩序。

branches.en: A wheel and a government can both turn around.
branches.cn: 轮子与政权都能转过来。

intro.en: Revolution combines re-, back, the root volv, to roll, and the noun suffix -ion.
intro.cn: revolution 由 re-（回）、词根 volv（滚）与名词后缀 -ion 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin revolvere and revolutio give the word its full shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 revolvere 与 revolutio 赋予这个词完整形态。

items.meaning: a gun with a turning part
items.example: Revolver comes from the same turning root.
items.exampleCN: revolver 来自同一个表示转动的词根。

latinEntries.example: Revolvere leads to the noun revolutio.

definition_zh: 职业；行业；同业；声明；信仰表白
definition_en: a job that needs special training and a formal qualification, the people who do it, or an open declaration of belief
core_image: 一个人站在众人面前，一手按在胸前，公开说出自己以什么为业、又信什么
scene: 面试官问她靠什么谋生，她说自己受过多年训练，做的是需要执照的活儿。 She practises the legal profession in a small coastal town.
sceneCN: 这里表示「需要专门训练的职业」（第 1 个义项：以长期训练和正式资格为基础的谋生行当）；句意为她在一座海滨小城从事法律工作。

derivatives.zh: 由 profession 加 -al 构成，义为「职业的；专业人士」
由 professional 加 -ism 构成，义为「专业水准；职业精神」
与 profession 同出拉丁语 profiteri，义为「公开宣称；声称」

senses.title: A job that requires special training and qualifications
senses.definition: a type of work that needs long training and a formal qualification, such as law or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 需要长期训练与正式资格的工作，如法律或医学
senses.example: She chose teaching as her profession.
senses.exampleCN: 她选择教书作为自己的职业。
senses.why: The Latin source meant to declare openly; a profession is the work one publicly declares as one's own, not a task done quietly and unnamed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头意为「公开宣称」；职业就是一个人当众声明属于自己的那份工作，而不是默默无名地做的杂活。

senses.title: The whole group of people who do such work
senses.definition: all the people who work in one such field, considered as a body with shared standards
senses.definitionCN: 在某一此类领域工作的所有人，被视为拥有共同标准的一个整体
senses.example: The medical profession opposed the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 医学界反对这些新规定。
senses.why: If a profession is what each member declares, the same word can name the company of all who make that declaration.
senses.whyCN: 既然职业是每个成员公开认领的东西，同一个词也就能指所有做出这一认领的人所组成的群体。

senses.title: A solemn declaration of religious faith
senses.definition: a formal and public statement that one holds a particular religious belief
senses.definitionCN: 公开而正式地表明自己持守某一宗教信仰
senses.example: Her profession of faith was made before the whole congregation.
senses.exampleCN: 她在全体会众面前作了信仰表白。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the Latin verb meant to declare aloud, and the first things declared in that way were matters of belief.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：拉丁动词本义就是「大声声明」，而最早被这样声明的正是信仰上的事。

senses.title: An open claim about one's feelings or intentions
senses.definition: a statement in which someone openly claims to feel or intend something
senses.definitionCN: 某人公开声称自己有某种感受或打算的说法
senses.example: His profession of friendship did not convince anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他声称的友谊没能说服任何人。
senses.why: Once the word means a public declaration, it can carry any claim a person makes aloud, including one that others may doubt.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「公开声明」，它就能承载任何被人大声说出的主张，包括旁人未必相信的那种。

intro.en: Profession and professor grow from the same Latin verb, but one names the declared work and the other the person who declares it.
intro.cn: profession 与 professor 出自同一个拉丁动词，但前者指被公开认领的工作，后者指做这种公开宣称的人。

items.en: Fateri meant to confess or acknowledge, to say something about oneself that others could hear.
items.cn: fateri 意为承认、供认，是把自己身上的事说给别人听。

items.en: Pro- made it public: profiteri meant to declare openly, often a belief or a calling.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 使它变为公开：profiteri 意为公开声明，常指声明信仰或志业。

items.en: The noun professio was a public declaration, and in Roman law it could also be the declared occupation on which tax was paid.
items.cn: 名词 professio 指公开声明；在罗马法中也可指申报并据此纳税的职业。

items.en: Old French profession kept both the religious and the occupational senses and passed them to English.
items.cn: 古法语 profession 同时保留宗教与职业两种含义，并把它们传入英语。

items.en: English uses profession mainly for qualified work and its body, while the older sense of open declaration survives in phrases such as a profession of faith.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用 profession 指需要资格的工作及其群体，而「公开声明」的旧义仍保存在 a profession of faith 这类说法里。

note.en: The first group shows the same Latin verb and its family, including the word for the person who declares; the second gathers words for jobs and for formal statements.
note.cn: 第一组收同一拉丁动词及其词族，包括指「宣称者」的词；第二组收表示工作与正式陈述的词。

entries.definition: To state openly that one has a belief or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 公开表明自己持有某种信仰或感受。

entries.definition: A senior university teacher; literally one who declares publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 资深大学教师；字面义为公开宣称的人。

entries.definition: Relating to a profession, or a person who works in one.
entries.definitionCN: 与职业有关的；从事某一职业的人。

entries.definition: To admit something one would rather keep hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 承认本不愿让人知道的事；坦白。

entries.definition: The job by which a person earns money.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人谋生所从事的工作。

entries.definition: The whole course of a person's working life.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人整个职业生涯的历程。

entries.definition: A skilled job, especially one done with the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 需要手艺的工作，尤指手工行业。

entries.definition: A formal statement made in public.
entries.definitionCN: 在公开场合做出的正式陈述。

normalIntro.en: One Latin verb of public declaration runs through the whole family, which is why the same word can mean a job and a statement of belief.
normalIntro.cn: 一整族词都建立在同一个表示「公开声明」的拉丁动词上，所以同一个词既能指职业，也能指信仰声明。

normal.en: Fateri is to admit; pro- makes it public, so profiteri is to say openly who you are and what you do.
normal.cn: fateri 是承认，pro- 使之公开，所以 profiteri 就是当众说出自己是谁、做什么。

normal.en: A profession is the work you declare as yours; a professor is the person who declares and teaches.
normal.cn: profession 是你公开认领的工作；professor 是做公开声明并讲授的人。

normal.en: The medical profession means the doctors as a group, because the declared work gathers its members into one body.
normal.cn: the medical profession 指医生这个群体，因为被共同认领的工作把成员聚成了一个整体。

normal.en: A profession of faith keeps the old sense of a spoken declaration, not a job.
normal.cn: a profession of faith 保留的是「口头声明」的旧义，与工作无关。

normal.en: Professional adds -al to profession, turning the field into an adjective or into the person who belongs to it.
normal.cn: professional 在 profession 后加 -al，把这个领域变成形容词，或指属于该领域的人。

abstract.en: A job becomes a profession only when it is publicly named, which suggests that recognition is part of the work itself.
abstract.cn: 一份工作只有被公开命名才成为职业，这说明「被承认」本身就是这份工作的一部分。

abstract.en: The same word covers what you do and what you believe, because both are things you stand up and declare.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既覆盖你做什么，也覆盖你信什么，因为两者都是你站出来声明的东西。

abstract.en: A profession is a promise made in public: that is why its members are held to shared standards.
abstract.cn: 职业是一份当众做出的承诺，所以它的成员要受共同标准的约束。

examples.en: She entered the teaching profession at twenty-two.
examples.cn: 她二十二岁进入教师行业。

examples.en: His profession of loyalty sounded sincere.
examples.cn: 他声称的忠诚听起来很真诚。

examples.en: Members of the legal profession attended the hearing.
examples.cn: 法律界人士出席了听证会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若费神」——挑职业要费神，入错行更费神；记住 profession 是职业。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、公开）+ fateri（承认、供认）→ profiteri（公开声明）→ professio（声明、申报的职业），经古法语 profession 进入英语；与 professor 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a public declaration; from it come the declared job, the body of people who share that job, and the statement of belief or feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「公开声明」；由此分出被公开认领的职业、共享该职业的群体，以及信仰或情感的表白。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing before a crowd, naming aloud the work he does and the belief he holds.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在众人面前，大声说出自己所做的工作与所持的信念。

branches.en: a person naming a calling and a loyalty in the same breath
branches.cn: 同一次开口里既说出志业，也说出忠诚

branches.en: doctors closing ranks behind their common standards
branches.cn: 医生们以共同标准站成一体

branches.en: a congregation listening to a spoken creed
branches.cn: 会众聆听一段口头的信条

branches.en: a young woman choosing law after years of study
branches.cn: 年轻女子在多年学习后选择法律

branches.en: a claim of friendship that others quietly doubt
branches.cn: 旁人暗自怀疑的友谊表白

intro.en: A Latin verb of admitting, its public prefix, and the noun and adjective endings built on them hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「承认」的拉丁动词、表示公开的前缀，以及建立其上的名词与形容词词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
